title: PINS Caseworker
description:
Summary/Objective:

In partnership with the Jefferson County Department of Social Services (JCDSS), the Person’s In Need of Supervision (PINS) Caseworker provides intensive home and community-based preventative services for youth ages 11-18 who are at risk of out-of-home placement. The primary goal of the Program is to avoid out-of-home placement and family disruption in cases of serious child/youth misbehavior. The Program is designed to help youth identify the underlying issues which resulted in their behaviors and assist them in learning new skills to reduce their risk of school referrals, school truancy, and criminal behaviors while becoming productive members of the community. The Program helps youth develop appropriate coping skills to handle emotional stressors, and access necessary services within their community. The Caseworker will hold a caseload up to ten youth at a time.


Essential Functions:

  1. As assigned, maintains a caseload of referred/enrolled program youth
  2. Within 72 business hours of referral, conducting assessments and intake of referred youth and family
  3. Provides intensive home and community-based services to families
  4. Actively participates as part of the treatment team and in accordance with the treatment plan, makes referrals to outside agencies
  5. To monitor progress and compliance, obtains regular updates from all service providers
  6. Performs the basic accountability tasks related to the job including compiling and maintaining all necessary records
  7. Completes all documents required by CHJC and the Jefferson County Department of Social Services in a timely manner
  8. Assists in the collection of program data and satisfaction surveys
  9. As needed, attends Court hearings/proceedings, regular monthly meetings with JCDSS, school meetings and other activities
  10. Completes all necessary progress notes, discharge reports, as well as treatment plans. in the Electronic Medical Record (EMR)
  11. Assesses barriers to engagement of youth and family and uses problem solving strategies to overcome barriers
  12. Responds to crisis in the home and or community
  13. Provides in-school support as needed, assist youth in getting to school
  14. Facilitates/provides Life Skill education to all program youth, either in a group setting or individually
  15. To promote Community Service and Civic Engagement seek out volunteer opportunities for

Work Environment:

Works both in an office setting and off-site/during in-home visits with program participants

title: Cybersecurity Requirements and Data Protection Lead
description:
Job Details

New ideas are all around us, but only a few will change the world. That’s our focus at JPL. We ask the biggest questions, then search the universe for answers—literally. We build upon ideas that have guided generations, then share our discoveries to inspire generations to come. Your mission—your opportunity—is to seek out the answers that bring us one step closer. If you’re driven to discover, create, and inspire something that lasts a lifetime and beyond, you’re ready for JPL.

Located in Pasadena, California, JPL has a campus-like environment situated on 177 acres in the foothills of the San Gabriel Mountains and offers a work environment unlike any other: we inspire passion, foster innovation, build collaboration, and reward excellence.

As a senior leader within JPL’s Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GR&C) team, you will develop and maintain the cybersecurity requirements framework for JPL’s missions and business operations. You will support the JPL Privacy Manager and Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) Liaison, oversee the lifecycle of sensitive data and ensure alignment with NASA, federal, and international regulations.

Key Responsibilities:

Strategy & Policy: Develop and maintain JPL’s cybersecurity requirements framework and policies to support mission-critical functions.

Privacy & Data Protection: Provide oversight for sensitive data in support of JPL’s designated Privacy Manager and CUI Liaison; guide strategies for Data Loss Prevention (DLP), encryption, and "Privacy by Design."

Risk Management: Conduct comprehensive risk assessments across information and operational technology (IT/OT) systems, supply chains, acquisitions, and external subcontracts.

Compliance & Frameworks: Ensure institutional alignment with standards such as NIST 800-53, GDPR/CCPA, and CMMC; manage data mapping, classification, and ethical data usage.

Cross-Functional Leadership: Translate complex regulatory requirements into technical architectures by collaborating with legal, information technology, and mission leads.

Incident & Audit Support: Lead investigations into data breaches/disclosures and provide subject matter expertise for internal and external audits.

Required Qualifications:

  • Typically requires a bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Information Technology, or similar discipline with a minimum of 9 years of cybersecurity experience; master's degree in similar discipline with a minimum of 7 years of cybersecurity experience; or PhD in similar disciplines with a minimum of 5 years cybersecurity experience.

  • Mastery in two or more of the following areas: NIST RMF, privacy frameworks (GDPR/CCPA), or system development lifecycle (SDLC).

  • Proficiency with Splunk and DLP tools.

  • Significant experience in aerospace, ground data systems, or cloud-based mission environments.

  • Familiarity with Nessus and GR&C platforms (e.g., RSA Archer).

  • Must be a US Citizen.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Current CISSP, CIPP/US (Certified Information Privacy Professional), CISM, or CGEIT desired.

title: Head of Development Digital Delivery
description:
Job summary

Great technology starts with great leadership. Ofgem is looking for a people-first Head of Development Delivery and bring together our development community to create the culture, confidence and ambition needed to deliver outstanding digital services.

Ofgem is Great Britains independent energy regulator. Were at the forefront of change across the sector, driving toward Net Zero whilst protecting consumers, especially vulnerable people.

This is a permanent opportunity to put people at the heart of development across our Digital Delivery portfolio. Leading a team of talented Technical Leads who oversee around 45 development staff, youll have the scope to make a real difference to how our teams work, collaborate and succeed.

Were evolving how we approach digital, and youll be joining at an exciting time to help move that forward. From raising engineering standards and exploring new technologies, tools and AI, to finding better ways of working, youll have the freedom to challenge thinking, encourage innovation and help our development community reach its full potential.

Above all, this is about people. Youll build trust, create an environment where honest conversations can happen and give technical leaders the confidence and support to get the best from their teams. When things arent straightforward, youll bring people together, cutting through ambiguity and helping find a way forward.

To be considered, youll need significant experience leading software development teams through other technical leaders, alongside a strong track record of coaching, managing performance and creating high-performing, supportive cultures. Youll also have experience driving technology adoption and change, delivering engineering standards and communicating confidently with technical and non-technical stakeholders at every level.

In return, youll have the opportunity to lead talented people, explore emerging technology and shape a development culture thats ready for what comes next. Alongside the freedom to make your mark, youll enjoy an outstanding rewards package, plenty of flexibility and a working environment that supports you to perform at your best.

We have a critical purpose to drive the digital performance of the energy sector. Join us and help create the culture and capability that will enable Ofgem to deliver on that mission.

Read on and find out more.

Job description

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead, develop and inspire: Provide clear direction, coaching and performance management for 68 Technical Leads and creating strong career pathways for developers across the portfolio.
  • Enhance engineering standards and ways of working: (e.g., SDLC, coding standards, branching/release strategy, security and quality gates), ensuring consistent delivery across multiple teams and suppliers.
  • Provide leadership across the portfolio SLT: Influencing investment decisions, and ensuring development capability aligns to scheme priorities and wider organisational objectives.
  • Operational planning: Understand team strengths and gaps, allocate resources to projects, support prioritisation/scheduling, and manage dependencies across products and delivery streams.
  • Supporting supplier relationship management: Contributing to contract management, assuring quality of partner delivery, and embedding agreed standards and governance.
  • Drive continuous improvement through actionable metrics and feedback loops (e.g., DORA, defect trends, lead time, deployment frequency, service health), using insight to remove bottlenecks and raise performance.
  • Support effective delivery governance by working closely with Product, Delivery, Architecture, Security and Service Management teams to manage risk, assure outcomes, and communicate progress and issues clearly to senior non-technical stakeholders.
  • Lead the strategic adoption of AI-enabled engineering: Working closely with our Innovation lead to define where AI tooling adds value, establish safe/approved usage patterns, upskill teams, and evolve ways of working to improve developer productivity and quality (e.g., assisted coding, test generation, documentation, code review support)
  • Build and sustain a healthy engineering culture that supports inclusion, wellbeing, knowledge sharing and high performance, including contributing to hiring, onboarding, and succession planning for critical roles.

Key Outputs and Deliverables

  • A clear, communicated development practice strategy and operating model, including standards, governance and ways of working.
  • Improved consistency and quality across teams evidenced by measurable engineering metrics (e.g., lead time, deployment frequency, defect escape rate, incident trends, velocity, burndown).
  • A high-performing leadership layer across development, with strong Technical Leads, clear expectations, effective 1:1s, feedback, performance management and development plans.
  • Effective resource planning and allocation across priority schemes and products, with transparent capacity, skills coverage, and mitigation plans for gaps.
  • An agreed AI-enabled engineering roadmap (tools, guardrails, training, and adoption measures) that demonstrably improves developer experience, productivity, and quality.
  • Trusted relationships with senior stakeholders, with clear, timely communication of delivery health, risks, and trade-offs, and evidence of issues being addressed at pace.

Key Stakeholder Relationships

Internal

Deputy Directors, Technical leads, other members of the Digital Delivery portfolio, Corporate services technical resources.

External

Scheme participants and system users, energy suppliers, DESNZ, third-party software development partners, vendors, consultancies and any other relevant stakeholders.

Person specification

Essential Criteria

  • Significant people leadership experience, leading software development teams through other leaders (e.g., Engineering Managers/Tech Leads), with a strong track record of coaching, performance management and building high-performing, supportive cultures. (Lead).
  • Evidence of driving technology change and adoption (for example, introducing new tooling, automation or AI assisted engineering practices) with appropriate governance, learning and measurable benefits.
  • Proven ability to set and embed engineering standards and improve consistency across multiple teams (including quality, security, testing and release practices).
  • Demonstrable experience of operational leadership in a technology function, including prioritisation, capacity/resource planning, dependency management and working across multi-disciplinary teams.
  • Experience working with partners/suppliers (e.g., cosourcing, consultancies) and contributing to contract and performance management to assure quality outcomes.

Behaviours

We'll assess you against these behaviours during the selection process:

  • Seeing the Big Picture
  • Leadership
  • Delivering at Pace

Benefits

Alongside your salary of 63,443, OFGEM contributes 18,379 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).

Ofgem can offer you a comprehensive and competitive benefits package which includes; 30 days annual leave after 2 years; Excellent training and development opportunities; The opportunity to join the generous Civil Service pension which also includes a valuable range of benefits;hybrid working (currently 1 day a week in the office butthis is keptunderreview), flexible working hours and family friendly policies.Pluslots of other benefits including clean and bright offices based centrally, engaged networks and teams and an opportunity to contribute to our ambitious and important targets ofestablishinga Net Zero energy system by 2050. This exciting blend of professional challenge and personal rewardidentifiescareer opportunities at Ofgem as something to get excited about

Things you need to know

Artificial intelligence
Artificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance (opens in a new window) for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

This vacancy is using Success Profiles (opens in a new window) , and will assess your Behaviours and Experience.

You will then be asked to provide a 1250 word personalstatement evidencing how you meet the essentialskills and capabilities listed in the role profile. Please ensure youdemonstrateclearly, within your supporting statement, how you meet each of thecriteria listed in the role profile.In the event ofreceivinga large number ofapplications,an initialsift may take place on just thelead criteriaindicatedin the essential criteria.

title: MQ-28 Ground System Senior Software Engineer
description:
OPPORTUNITY:
The Boeing MQ-28 - Ghost Bat is a globally significant program delivering disruptive advantage to support Defence operational capabilities. Developed in partnership with the Royal Australian Air Force, it is the first military combat aircraft to be designed, manufactured and assembled in Australia in 50 years. In line with the global ambitions of the aircraft it is also the first (and currently only) CCA globally to fly outside of the country in which it was designed.MQ-28 is expanding globally with international customers and international design and partner network.
Position Overview:As a Senior Software Engineer specialising in the Ground System for the MQ-28 Ghost Bat project, you will play a critical role in the development, integration, and maintenance of software systems that support the launch, recovery and situational awareness of our advanced unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). You will collaborate with cross-functional teams to ensure the software system is robust, reliable, secure and capable of meeting mission requirements.
Key Responsibilities: * * Software Development: * Design, develop, and test software applications for ground control systems, including automation of Unit level tests, ensuring compliance with project standards. * Develop and support build pipelines and infrastructure and own your systems in production. * Integration and Testing: * Develop and lead software verification plans, test procedures and test environments, executing the test procedures and documenting test results to ensure software system requirements are met. * Conduct rigorous testing and verification of software to ensure performance, reliability, and security. * System Maintenance: * Monitor and troubleshoot software issues, providing timely resolutions to maintain system integrity. * Perform regular updates and enhancements to existing software systems based on user feedback and evolving mission requirements. * Documentation: * Create and maintain comprehensive documentation for software design, development processes, and user manuals. * Ensure all documentation is up-to-date and accessible for team members and stakeholders. * Collaboration: * Work closely with other engineering disciplines, including systems engineering, safety and airworthiness, cybersecurity, and user experience, to deliver integrated solutions. * Contribute and be prepared to lead agile ceremonies, actively participate in daily stand-ups, retrospectives, Program Increment planning and other team meetings. * With general direction perform design reviews, code reviews, and technical meetings to share knowledge and improve team performance. * Develop supplier/subcontract performance assessment including appropriate metrics. Make recommendations of adequacy of subcontractor/supplier technical approach to project lead. * Contributes to the completion of specific programs and projects. Failure to obtain results, reaching erroneous decisions or making recommendations would typically result in serious program delays and considerable expenditure of resources * Mentor less experienced team members * Research and Development: * Stay current with emerging technologies and industry trends related to UAV ground systems and software engineering. * Contribute to research initiatives aimed at improving the capabilities and efficiency of the MQ-28 Ghost Bat ground systems. Qualifications: * Education: Degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field. * Experience: * Minimum of 8 years of experience in software development, with a focus on Aerospace or Defence systems preferred (Essential). * Proficiency in programming languages such as C++, C# or Python (Essential). * Experience with software development methodologies (Agile, Scrum) and tools (Git, JIRA) (Highly Desirable). * Experience in the Aerospace industry (Highly Desirable). * Experience with design and development work with Human Machine Interfaces (UX/UI) (Highly Desirable). * Skills: * Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work independently and as part of a team (Essential). * Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written (Essential). * Familiarity with ground control systems and UAV operations (Highly Desirable). * Independently determines and develops approaches to solutions. Receives general direction for work that is reviewed upon completion for adequacy in meeting objectives (Essential). * Security Clearance: Ability to obtain and maintain a minimum of an NV1 level security clearance (Essential). Working Conditions: * This position may require occasional travel to support field testing and customer engagements. * Work may be performed in a combination of office and lab environments. What's on offer?
We are a business that evolves by encouraging our people to grow, so you will bring a mindset, behaviour and skills to improve the business, processes and yourself. This will see you thrive and achieve the organisation goals whilst being focused on your personal development through formal and informal learning.
We value the health and wellbeing of our employees and offer true flexibility including working from home, compressed work weeks, and opportunities for part time arrangements, allowing you to balance your career with what is important to you outside of work. We will celebrate your successes and achievements with a formal reward and recognition program and employee awards.
Other benefits * Work on cutting edge projects; * Attractive remuneration and annual bonus; * Formal mentoring and training as well as on the job learning; * Access discounts for health insurance, travel and accommodation; * Paid study leave, parental leave, Defence leave and First Nation's Cultural Leave; * Salary packaging options available; * Health and wellbeing benefits including annual flu vaccinations and Employee Assistance Program; * Join social and community groups; and * We explore opportunities to engage with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander programs and initiatives focusing on STEM engagements. title: AI Governance Lead
description:
We’re the airline that dares to be different, bold, down-to-earth and built around giving our guests real choice. Safety is our backbone, service is our heartbeat, and our people are our superpower.

At Virgin Australia, we’re on a mission to be Australia’s most loved airline, for our people, our guests and our owners, and we’re looking for passionate talent to help take us even higher.

We’re vibrant, authentic and unapologetically human. Here, you can bring your whole self, your Virgin Flair and your ambition to a team that champions individuality, innovation and a whole lot of heart. If you’re excited by meaningful work, real opportunities to grow, and a culture where you can genuinely make a difference, you’ll feel right at home with us.

Your Impact

In our Legal, Ethics and Governance Office, we help Virgin Australia do the right thing, in the right way, while enabling the business to move forward with confidence. We bring together sound judgement, practical governance and a clear focus on managing risk without creating unnecessary complexity.

As AI Governance Lead, you’ll play a key role in embedding practical, proportionate and sustainable governance for the responsible use of artificial intelligence across Virgin Australia Group. Reporting to the General Manager, Ethics and Compliance, you’ll provide enterprise-wide governance leadership, oversight and advice, helping ensure AI risks are identified, assessed, managed, monitored and escalated through the right business processes and governance forums.

This is an opportunity to take established AI governance arrangements and make them work effectively in business as usual. Rather than designing AI solutions or owning technical delivery, your focus will be on operating, embedding, maintaining and continuously improving the governance approach, while supporting clear accountability and informed decision-making.

You’ll work across the Group with the AI Centre of Excellence, Technology, Risk, Legal, Privacy, Information Security, Internal Audit and business leaders. Your work will help shape how AI is responsibly used in a highly regulated, safety-critical airline environment.

You’ll be involved in everything from AI use case intake, risk assessment and approvals through to ongoing monitoring, reporting, assurance and continuous improvement. You’ll also help maintain the Group’s AI inventory and risk information, coordinate governance forums and provide clear, practical advice to leaders and business owners.

Importantly, you’ll help make AI governance accessible and workable for the business by developing practical guidance, tools and communications, supporting capability uplift and keeping the organisation ready to respond as technology, regulation and external expectations continue to evolve.

About You

You’ll bring experience in AI governance and governance of automated or data-driven systems. You will have a depth of exposure in governance, risk, compliance and technology risk, ideally gained in a complex or regulated organisation. You’ll be comfortable operating governance frameworks in a business-as-usual environment and working with senior leaders, governance forums and diverse stakeholders.

You’ll have a practical approach to risk and governance, with the ability to take complex regulatory, technology or risk considerations and turn them into clear, workable processes and advice. You’ll be confident making sound judgements in areas where the answer is not always straightforward and know how to influence without adding unnecessary bureaucracy.

You’ll be a clear and credible communicator, able to prepare executive and committee materials, facilitate conversations and build productive relationships across functions. You’ll also bring an analytical mindset, good attention to detail and the ability to manage competing priorities while maintaining accurate governance records and follow-through.

A relevant tertiary qualification in law, risk, governance, technology, data, business or a related discipline is expected. Knowledge of enterprise risk management, governance, controls, assurance and ethics and compliance principles will be important, along with an understanding of the AI lifecycle and the ethical, legal, regulatory, privacy, security and safety considerations that come with emerging technologies.

Your Benefits & Beyond

We’re committed to looking after you, with some of the best benefits and conditions in the industry, including:

  • Discounted flights for you and your loved ones, including $1,000 worth of travel credits each year
  • A flexible, hybrid work style, with the ability to work from home or the office and adapt your location to suit your role and needs
  • One of Brisbane’s most admired head office locations, with South Bank train station, a supermarket, pharmacy and lunch options downstairs, plus easy access to the Busway, rooftop dining, onsite gym and South Bank Parklands
  • Discounts on travel insurance, lounge membership, car hire, accommodation and experiences worldwide
  • Cheaper hospitality, retail, technology, beauty and wellness services
  • Free counselling and access to a wellbeing app supporting your physical, mental, social and financial wellbeing
  • ‘Dress for Your Day’, giving you the freedom to wear what makes sense for the work you’re doing

Belonging at Virgin Australia

We’re all individuals. And we love that. That’s why we encourage applications from Indigenous Australians, people with disability, those from diverse cultural backgrounds, our friends in the LGBTQI+ community, and anyone else who wants to join our family.

Ready to apply?

We’re ready to hear from you. Apply now.

title: Building Services Supervisor: UT Space Institute
description:
The University of Tennessee Space Institute (UTSI) seeks a Building Services Supervisor to provide day-to-day leadership and operational oversight for custodial services across the campus. Reporting to the Group Director of Facilities, this position supervises assigned custodial employees, develops and adjusts work schedules, assigns and monitors work, trains staff, evaluates performance, and helps ensure consistent service across academic, administrative, research, event, and common-use facilities.

The supervisor also performs and supports custodial work as needed, inspects completed work, maintains cleaning and safety standards, identifies facility or equipment concerns, monitors custodial supplies and equipment, and ensures the proper use of cleaning chemicals, tools, and personal protective equipment. The position responds to changing campus priorities and supports reliable, safe, efficient, and professional custodial services throughout UTSI.

Supervision, Scheduling, Work Orders, and Administrative Coordination (40%)

  • Supervise assigned custodial staff responsible for services across UTSI campus buildings.

  • Develop daily, weekly, and periodic cleaning schedules; adjust assignments based on staffing, events, service priorities, and campus needs.

  • Assign, monitor, and follow up on custodial work orders and service requests through the University’s work order or computerized maintenance management system (CMMS).

  • Train and retrain employees in custodial procedures, equipment operation, chemical safety, personal protective equipment, work order procedures, customer service expectations, and departmental standards.

  • Monitor performance, conduct evaluations, provide coaching and feedback, approve time, monitor attendance, and address performance or conduct concerns in coordination with the Group Director of Facilities.

  • Participate in hiring, interviews, onboarding, disciplinary recommendations, and other personnel actions as appropriate.

  • Maintain operational records and communicate regularly with the Group Director of Facilities regarding staffing, service levels, employee concerns, supplies, building conditions, and customer requests.

Custodial Operations (40%)

  • Perform and support routine custodial work in offices, classrooms, restrooms, laboratories, conference areas, common spaces, event spaces, and other assigned campus facilities.

  • Sweep, mop, vacuum, dust, clean and sanitize restrooms, remove trash and recycling, restock supplies, and complete other routine cleaning tasks as needed.

  • Perform or assist with floor care, carpet extraction, deep cleaning, emergency cleanup, odor- or pest-related cleaning support, and event setup or cleanup.

  • Operate custodial tools and equipment, including vacuums, carts, buffers, scrubbers, extractors, and related equipment.

  • Assist with moving furniture, equipment, supplies, and materials to support campus events, office moves, facility needs, and daily operations.

  • Respond to spills, urgent cleaning needs, service requests, and special assignments promptly and professionally.

Quality Control, Safety, and Inventory (10%)

  • Inspect buildings, restrooms, common areas, and completed assignments to ensure cleaning, safety, and campus appearance standards are met; follow up on corrective action when needed.

  • Identify and report maintenance problems, unsafe conditions, damaged equipment, pest or odor concerns, and other facility needs.

  • Ensure cleaning chemicals, tools, supplies, and equipment are used, stored, and secured properly, and enforce safe work practices and required personal protective equipment.

  • Monitor supply inventory and equipment condition, request replenishment, and assist with product evaluation or vendor coordination as needed.

Special Projects and Other Duties (10%)

  • Support periodic custodial projects, special cleaning assignments, conferences, and event-related custodial needs.

  • Coordinate with other Facilities and Infrastructure staff to support maintenance activities, events, emergency response, and overall campus operations.

  • Perform other duties consistent with the scope and intent of the position.

Required Qualifications

Education:

  • High school diploma or GED

Experience:

  • At least three years of relevant experience in custodial services, building services, facilities operations, institutional maintenance, or a closely related field, including at least one year of supervisory, lead-worker, or work-direction experience.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Knowledge of custodial operations, cleaning methods, cleaning chemicals, equipment use, and safe work practices.

  • Skill in supervising, directing, training, and evaluating the work of others.

  • Skill in planning, organizing, prioritizing, and coordinating daily work across multiple buildings or work areas.

  • Ability to work cooperatively and coordinate effectively with supervisors, coworkers, customers, and other campus personnel.

  • Ability to use basic computer systems, email, electronic timekeeping, Microsoft Office, and work order or CMMS systems.

  • Ability to read, understand, and follow oral and written instructions, safety data sheets, procedures, work orders, and schedules.

  • Ability to exercise sound judgment, resolve routine operational issues, and refer complex matters to the Group Director of Facilities.

  • Ability to safely perform custodial work involving prolonged standing and walking, repetitive motion, bending, reaching, climbing, and lifting or moving materials and equipment weighing up to 50 pounds.

  • Skill in safely using, inspecting, and performing routine operator maintenance on custodial tools and equipment.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience:

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Knowledge of custodial operations in a campus, institutional, research, industrial, or similar multi-building environment.

  • Knowledge of custodial considerations for laboratories, technical workspaces, event spaces, offices, classrooms, and public-facing facilities.

  • Skill in coaching employees, resolving routine workplace issues, and supporting a positive, service-oriented team culture.

  • Skill in improving work processes, staffing efficiency, cleaning schedules, safety practices, and customer service outcomes.

Work Location and Conditions

  • Location: University of Tennessee Space Institute, Tullahoma, Tennessee

  • Work arrangement: Onsite

  • Schedule: First shift, with occasional evening and weekend work

  • This position is designated as essential personnel for emergencies and may be required to report when the University has suspended or delayed operations.

  • Must be legally authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis without need now or in the future for sponsorship for employment-based visa status.

  • Employment is contingent upon successful completion of required background screening, drug screening, and security clearance checks.

Compensation and Benefits

  • UT market range: MR07

  • Anticipated hiring range: $50,000 - $55,000

The University of Tennessee Space Institute is a graduate education and research institution located in Tullahoma, Tennessee. UTSI advances education, research, and innovation in aerospace, engineering, science, and related fields through collaboration with the Tickle College of Engineering, university partners, government agencies, industry, and the surrounding community. Facilities and Infrastructure supports the safe, reliable, and effective operation of the campus and the specialized environments that serve UTSI’s academic and research mission.

Locally, we are a small family environment, and nationally, as part of Comfort Systems USA, we are one the largest Mechanical Contractors with excellent benefits packages, competitive pay structures, career progression, and more.

Job Title: Field Foreman (Plumbing)

Department: Construction

Reports to: Labor Manager

Location: Louisville, CO (projects throughout the Denver metro area)

Job Type: Full -Time

FLSA Status: Non-Exempt (eligible for OT)
Wage Range: $33-40+/hour (Depending on experience)

Benefits Included: Comprehensive Medical, Dental, Vision, FSA/HSA, Matching 401K, Long Term Disability, Short Term Disability, Company Paid Life & Voluntary Spouse & Child Insurance, AD&D, Employee Assistance Program, PTO, Paid Holidays, voluntary additional insurances/benefits, and other great perks.

Job Description:
The Plumbing Foreman ensures the Safety of those we work with and around, the Quality of the services we provide, and the realization of our Profitability goals as it specifically relates to the commercial installation, assembly, and repairs on a variety of mechanical plumbing systems. The Foreman will work closely with the Project Team to ensure all projects are completed according to the project documents, adhering to the project budget and the planned schedule. This position is also responsible for understanding all aspects of project documentation and installation of the plumbing trade, using knowledge and experience in the trade along with management skills to coordinate internal people and external clients. This may include hands on work in the trade.

Responsibilities:

  • Work with the project team to ensure we are familiar with contract inclusions, scope of work, proposal, and any accepted value engineering options

  • Know your plans, specifications, contract schedule, and budget

  • Ensure your team is familiar with and using the most current set of contract documents, including all mechanical/plumbing details

  • Be familiar with budgeted hours and work with the project manager and team members to identify and implement any cost-saving strategies. Work with the project manager for change order pricing, ensuring we are capturing all costs. Utilize prefabrication. Know and understand your crew cost

  • Make sure you are aware of schedule changes and make necessary adjustments to manpower and material needs. Work directly with the project manager to develop and maintain a 3-week manpower look ahead and update weekly

  • Ensure Design Mechanical's core values are always implemented and that the company's safety policies and procedures are always followed

  • Ensure that systems are installed to the highest degree of quality and functionality

  • Maintain a positive working relationship with clients, vendors, and colleagues. Provide solutions when called upon. Deliver a quality product on time and within budget

  • Communicate expectations and expect accountability. When expectations are not being met, address the issue with the individual to determine appropriate action, training, or disciplinary action

  • Ensure crews are properly laid out, organized, and productive

  • Attend all appropriate meetings, including pre-plan and weekly subcontractor coordination meetings

  • Work with project managers to pre-plan your project and understand specific equipment & materials being used

  • Take an active role in the BIM/CAD process:

    • If the project is modeled, work closely with the CAD department to ensure we are using the right products and producing a buildable model

    • Create a prefabrication plan with the prefab coordinator and the fab shop. Create and maintain a batching schedule with the CAD department and the fab shop

    • Be sure we are using the most current information from the BIM coordination and always reference contract drawings

  • Implement and maintain a QA/QC plan. Ensure that all systems are installed per plans, specifications, and current and local codes

  • Ensure all systems requiring testing are tested and documented

  • Ensure that all systems are installed to the highest quality and functionality standards

  • Ensure that project is properly documented with daily reports, pressure testing reports, enter crew members' time, disciplinary actions, etc.

  • Maintain accurate as-built drawings throughout the project

  • Request appropriate inspections and documents appropriately

Qualifications:

  • Minimum Journeyman license in respective trade (Plumbing: Journeyworker Plumber License)

  • Foreman will have 3-5+ years of experience running commercial mechanical projects ranging from $1-10M in value

  • Computer skills required, with a good working knowledge of all Microsoft Office applications

  • Effective interpersonal skills are required for a strong representation of DMI customers as well as employees

  • Valid CO Driver’s License and Clear MVR

  • Can successfully pass a criminal background check, drug test, and physical ensuring you can perform the duties of the job

  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to:

    • Arrive at each job site on time and at the specified time

    • Have a full range of mobility in the upper and lower body

    • Be able to reach overhead

    • Be able to work a full range of physical activities in various positions, including, but not limited to, standing, bending over, kneeling and squatting, climbing, walking for extended periods of time

    • Be able to lift, pull and push materials and equipment to complete assigned job tasks

    • Be able to lift 50-70 pounds of weight throughout the assigned workday

    • Capable of hearing at a level or correctable to a level where the person can receive detailed information through verbal communication. Vision must also be at a level or correctable level where the person has clarity both in short and long-distance vision

Work Environment:

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly exposed to:

  • Outdoor weather conditions (dirt, temperature extremes, dampness, lightning, ice, snow)

  • Loud noise levels

  • Jobsite conditions (vibrations, equipment movement, hazards, chemicals and solvents)

  • Work at night and in the dark

The person will be expected to be free from fear of heights and can work at heights on ladders and scaffolds. Some work may occur in confined spaces.

This Job Description is not a complete statement of all duties and responsibilities comprising this position and may change with or without notice.

title: Projectleider Architectuur
description:
Ontwerp slimme oplossingen en realiseer impactvolle verandering

“Architectuur gaat voor mij over meer dan een goed ontwerp. Het gaat over samenwerken, keuzes maken en zorgen dat een idee uiteindelijk ook echt gerealiseerd kan worden. Als projectleider verbind je ontwerp, techniek en opdrachtgever en geef je samen met je team richting aan het proces. Juist die combinatie maakt deze rol interessant.”

— Emiel Hengst - BUM Architectuur

Werken bij Sweco betekent dat je onderdeel wordt van het grootste architecten- en ingenieursnetwerk van Europa. Je hebt de kennis van ruim 24.000 collega’s met één druk op de knop binnen handbereik. Onze business unit Architectuur in Nederland bestaat uit 75 collega’s, verspreid over Maastricht, Eindhoven, Utrecht. Samen werken we aan een bijzondere mix van projecten: van woningbouw en zorg tot complexe opgaven binnen de hightech maakindustrie en leisure. Juist die grote variatie maakt het werk interessant want het ene moment werk je aan een gebouw voor de zorg, het volgende aan een complexe hightech omgeving waarin techniek, architectuur en functionaliteit nauw samenkomen. Als projectleider beweeg je je daardoor steeds tussen verschillende vraagstukken, opdrachtgevers en disciplines en werk je samen met architecten, engineers, BIM-specialisten en andere experts aan gebouwen die écht ergens over gaan.

Als projectleider architectuur ben jij de verbindende schakel tussen opdrachtgever, architecten, engineers en andere betrokken disciplines. Je bewaakt de voortgang en kwaliteit van projecten, houdt de communicatielijnen helder en zet samen met de senior engineer de engineering uit. Je onderhoudt het contact met opdrachtgevers, bespreekt inhoudelijke en financiële vraagstukken en bent ook gesprekspartner wanneer er sprake is van meerwerk. Daarbij houd je overzicht over het proces en zorg je dat ontwerp en engineering goed op elkaar aansluiten. BIM speelt hierin een belangrijke rol: we werken voortdurend aan het verder verhogen van de kwaliteit van onze ontwerpen en processen. Heb je al ruime ervaring als projectleider, dan krijg je volop ruimte om verantwoordelijkheid te nemen. Heb je minder ervaring, maar spreekt deze rol je aan en wil je hierin groeien? Ook dan nodigen we je nadrukkelijk uit om te solliciteren. We kijken niet alleen naar wat je al kunt, maar ook naar de stap die je wilt maken.

Je krijgt bij Sweco de ruimte om je verder te ontwikkelen, zowel als projectleider als binnen de architectuur. Je werkt aan projecten met verschillende schaalgroottes en opdrachtgevers en kunt samenwerken met specialisten vanuit allerlei disciplines. Daarnaast is er ruimte om je verder te verdiepen in BIM, projectmanagement of juist een andere richting binnen het vak. We zoeken iemand die verantwoordelijkheid durft te nemen, graag samenwerkt en energie krijgt van het realiseren van goede ontwerpen. Of je nu al jaren projecten leidt of klaar bent om die volgende stap te zetten: we gaan graag met je in gesprek over wat jij kunt bijdragen én waar jij naartoe wilt groeien.

[sweco-recruitee-vacancy-summary]

Dit is wat we jou bieden

Bij Sweco zit je goed. Dit mag je verwachten van een werkgever met het World-class Workplace label. Om te beginnen ontvang je conform CAO voor Architectenbureaus een goed salaris en 30 vakantiedagen. Daarnaast bieden we een thuiswerkvergoeding, vakantietoeslag, een circulaire thuiswerkplek en een goede pensioenregeling.

Daarnaast krijg je bij Sweco veel regie, vrijheid en verantwoordelijkheid. Over hoeveel je werkt, waar je werkt, hoe je werkt en wanneer je werkt. Binnen ons arbeidsvoorwaardenpakket heb je de keuze om te kiezen op welke manier jij reist. We stimuleren duurzame en actieve keuzes en belonen deze extra. Ook krijg je direct toegang tot onze eigen AI-omgeving SwecoGPT, tot de Sweco Academy voor zeer ruime ontwikkelmogelijkheden, en tot ons vitaliteitsprogramma gericht op leefstijl en sport.

Naast uitdagend werk, support en middelen pakken we bij Sweco ook graag uit als het gaat om ontspanning en lol. We willen graag dat je met veel plezier naar je werk gaat. Denk aan een tweedaags event voor alle nieuwe collega’s, de dagelijkse Fika’s op kantoor, events op jouw vestiging, en activiteiten vanuit Jong Sweco en de lokale personeelsverenigingen.

Solliciteer op deze functie

Enthousiast geworden? Solliciteer dan direct via de button ‘solliciteren’. We kijken uit naar je cv en motivatie!

Neem bij inhoudelijke vragen of interesse in Sweco contact op met Emiel Hengst, BUM Architectuur via emiel.hengst@sweco.nl. Vragen over het sollicitatieproces kun je stellen aan Bert aan den Toorn via +31 6 39 44 05 98 of bert.aandentoorn@sweco.nl.

**Acquisitie stellen wij niet op prijs**

  • Een afgeronde hbo- of wo-opleiding in architectuur, bouwkunde of vergelijkbaar

  • Minimaal 10 jaar ervaring binnen de bouwbranche

  • Affiniteit met BIM en digitale ontwerp- en werkprocessen; kennis van Revit is een pre.

  • Je bent communicatief sterk en kunt goed schakelen tussen opdrachtgever, ontwerp en engineering.

  • Je neemt verantwoordelijkheid, werkt graag samen en wilt jezelf blijven ontwikkelen.

title: Customer Engineer (German speaking)
description:
About Open

Open.cx is the AI customer experience platform, automating support, outbound, sales, and customer understanding, built for enterprises that cannot afford slow, expensive, or mediocre support. We automate over 80% of interactions for companies like MoneyGram, Mollie, TicketSwap, and More.com handling voice, email, and web at massive scale with AI that thinks fast and feels human.

We are backed by Y Combinator, Pioneer Fund, X by Unifonic. We recently raised $7M+ and are accelerating from a startup into a global scale-up. Our customers replace entire stacks of legacy tools, cut support costs by up to 12×, and deliver dramatically better experiences to their own customers.

We are a small, high-output team that ships fast, works directly with customers, and genuinely cares about the product we are building.

The Role

We are hiring a Customer Engineer to serve as the direct technical bridge between our enterprise customers and the Open.cx product. This is a hands-on engineering role with heavy customer exposure not pure support, and not pure internal development.

You will respond quickly to customer queries via Slack or video calls, lead onboarding and implementation, debug complex issues including third-party integrations, and ship fixes or enhancements directly in our Node.js + TypeScript codebase. Prompt engineering is a significant part of the role you will help customers get the most out of our AI agents capabilities every day.

What You'll Do

  • Primary Technical Point of Contact: Respond fast to customer queries, join video calls, and own resolution end-to-end.
  • Lead Technical Onboarding: Guide enterprise customers through setup, configuration, and integration with tools like Zendesk, Intercom, HubSpot, and others.
  • Debug & Troubleshoot: Diagnose and resolve complex issues in live customer environments.
  • Ship Code: Implement fixes, integration enhancements, and small features directly in the Node.js / TypeScript codebase.
  • Collaborate with Product Engineering: Share customer context, escalate systemic problems, and help prioritise what the team builds next.
  • Develop Platform Expertise: Build deep knowledge of our AI agents and prompt engineering so you can effectively advise customers on optimising their support operations.
  • Document & Scale Knowledge: Document recurring issues, solutions, and integration patterns to strengthen internal knowledge and customer resources.

Requirements

What We're Looking For

  • Native or professional fluency in German (spoken and written).
  • 2-3+ years of experience Strong software engineering experience with Node.js and TypeScript you will be writing and shipping production code.
  • Hands-on experience with AI agents and prompt engineering (Open.cx is AI-native; this is core to the role).
  • Previous customer-facing technical work: onboarding, debugging integrations, or similar in a SaaS environment.
  • Good understanding of (or fast ability to learn) helpdesk APIs: Zendesk, Intercom, HubSpot, etc.
  • Excellent English communication clear writing and confident speaking on video calls with enterprise stakeholders.
  • Ability to operate effectively in a fast-moving startup: speed, customer impact, and getting things done.
  • Able to be working with customers across US, EU, MENA and GCC time zones.

Benefits

What We Offer

  • YC-backed with real traction we are in-market, growing, and trusted by enterprise names you know.
  • Outsized career trajectory early team members grow into leadership as we scale globally.
  • Real ownership your work will be seen, felt, and talked about company-wide.
  • High-trust team no politics, no bureaucracy; we move fast and support each other.
  • Competitive compensation top-of-market salary plus equity and full benefits.

title: Commercial Driver – Full Time

AutoZone offers career stability and growth opportunities in an essential industry. Plus, no Commercial Driver’s License (CDL) is required, and you’ll use company-provided vehicles!
  • Customer Service Excellence & Communication – Deliver WOW! Customer Service by engaging with commercial customers and DIY shoppers, providing clear and professional automotive advice and offering installation services.
  • Leadership & Teamwork – Work closely with store personnel and commercial accounts, ensuring smooth team collaboration and strong customer relationships.

Testing & Specimen Preparation

title: Data Governance Lead
description:
Data Governance Lead
£75,000 · Permanent · North West, hybrid
Build enterprise data governance from a standing start, for a UK listed group, with the executive team already behind you.

Most data governance roles have already made decisions, and the role is already decided. This one is slightly different.
A UK listed group is building enterprise data governance from scratch and looking for the person to design it, run it and be accountable for it. Not to administer a framework somebody else wrote, but to decide what the framework is.

Background

Governance has been tried here before and it did not stick, for a reason worth being honest about: there was no executive backing. That has changed, and changed hard.
Data governance is now a named material business control under Provision 29 of the UK Corporate Governance Code, with a board level attestation deadline in March. It is reported in the annual report. The CFO, who has done this before and understands controls properly, owns the agenda. The four priority data domains have already been signed off at executive level. Senior stakeholders are currently asking the hiring manager what they can do to help.
That is an unusual starting position, and it is the difference between a governance role that produces a policy library nobody reads and one that changes how a large business runs.
The scope
Four data domains, customer, product, colleague and clinical, across a group carrying UK GDPR obligations, FCA regulated activity and sector specific clinical regulation. Genuinely varied data, genuinely different control requirements, at real scale.
In year one you will design a proportionate framework, work out which data actually matters, land the policies, agree ownership, build a working steward network across the business, and produce the evidence the board needs to attest.
You will not fix everything by March and nobody expects you to. What is wanted is a minimum viable framework that proves its value and can be built on. The ambition after that is significant: catalogue, master data, lineage, and in time the governance of AI as the technology roadmap matures.

One thing to be clear about
There is no tooling budget in year one.
This is deliberate. The organisation wants value demonstrated first and a business case for a platform built on evidence, not on faith. If your first ninety days depend on selecting a catalogue vendor, this is not your role. If you can make meaningful progress with a spreadsheet, a good argument and the right people in the room, read on.

Who this is actually for
The technical bar matters. The human bar matters more.
This role lives or dies on whether you can walk into a room of senior people who did not ask for you, explain why this matters in language they recognise, and leave with them on your side. Then do it again next week with a different team who are busy and unconvinced.
You will need to tell a director their data is wrong without damaging the relationship. Hold your position when somebody senior pushes back. Make governance feel useful to the person doing it, not just compliant. Be pragmatic about what gets done first, and confident enough to defend what you have chosen not to do.
You will work closely with the Director of Engineering and his data team, so you need enough technical depth to hold your own, without becoming the technology’s advocate rather than the business’s.

What we are looking for
• Hands on experience building or substantially extending a data governance framework in a large, complex organisation, whether you owned all of it or led a major part of it
• A track record of establishing data ownership and running cross functional steward groups that actually changed behaviour
• Practical data quality experience, processes, metrics and reporting, connected to commercial outcomes
• Strong working knowledge of UK GDPR and information security principles
• The credibility to influence and challenge at senior level, and the resilience to keep going when it is slow

Helpful, not essential
• Regulated environment exposure: financial services, healthcare, clinical or similar
• DAMA CDMP, DCAM or CIPP/E
• Experience evidencing controls to auditors
• An interest in AI governance. Expertise is not needed, curiosity is

Sector experience is not required. How you work with people is.

Practical
Salary £75,000
Team Solo lead role initially, with an analyst expected to follow, and a genuine path towards a broader data and AI governance remit.
Location Hybrid with no mandated office days, but you need to be North West based and willing to be in regularly. This job is built on relationships and they do not form over Teams.
Process Two stages, moving quickly. Your first conversation is with me, recorded, so you get a proper briefing before you commit to anything.
To apply
Contact Sam Mikkelsen at True Worth Consulting on sam@trueworthconsulting.com. Happy to have an off the record conversation first if you would rather understand the business before putting your name to anything.

title: Associate Scientist - Dermatology
description:
The Kimberly and Eric J. Waldman Department of Dermatology at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai is dedicated to delivering superior, comprehensive dermatologic care that exceeds patient expectations, and to advancing the science of dermatology through research and education.

From preparing the next generation of leaders, to providing cutting-edge and cost-effective treatment, the Department of Dermatology thrives on a passion to improve the lives of patients through science.

The Associate Scientist is experienced in the conduct of research involving the understanding of human diseases and improvement of human health. May assist in the operation of the clinical laboratory. Engages in clinical investigation or other research, production, technical writing, and related activities, and may mentor less senior scientist and Associate Researcher staff.

  • Conducts research to develop methodologies, instrumentation and procedures for medical application, analyzing data and presenting findings.
  • Designs and conducts complex clinical research studies requiring the determination and evaluation of alternative methods, computational modeling, diagnosis and treatment.
  • Plans and directs studies to investigate human or animal disease, preventive methods, and treatments for disease.
  • May assist in clinical laboratory operations.
  • Follows strict safety procedures when handling materials to avoid contamination.
  • Teaches principles of medicine and medical and laboratory procedures to physicians, residents, students, and research staff.
  • Confers with health departments, industry personnel, physicians, and others to develop health safety standards and public health improvement programs.
  • Develops treatments and designs research tools and techniques.
  • Explores subject area and defines scope and selection of problems for investigation through conceptually related studies.
  • Develops hypotheses to be tested and methodology for evaluating results.

title: Agent Engineering Intern
description:
Los Altos, CA · Engineering · Internship · Semester/quarter or summer · Fully in-person

Company Overview

Cheiron recently raised an $8M seed round led by Menlo Ventures, and now has $13M total raised. The round also included strategic support from Moderna co-founder Robert Langer, former Pfizer Chief Medical Officer Freda Lewis-Hall, Chai Discovery co-founder and CEO Josh Meier, former Starbucks CEO Laxman Narasimhan, and former Apple AI chief John Giannandrea.

Cheiron is building the first AI-native operating system designed to represent an entire drug program as a single connected system. The platform helps biopharma teams represent, reason over, and stress-test the claims, evidence, decisions, and commitments, driving the drug program to completion.

About the Role

We're looking for an Agent Engineering Intern to build new agent-driven workflows inside Cheiron's product.

Cheiron's agents do more than generate an answer. They break complex objectives into steps, retrieve evidence, call tools, maintain state across long-running work, recover from failures, and produce structured results that a person can review and trust. You will own a bounded workflow and help take it from an ambiguous problem to a reliable, working product.

This is an applied engineering role, not an AI research internship. We care about strong software fundamentals, hands-on ownership, and evidence that you have built nontrivial systems yourself. The role is best suited to undergraduate and master's students who are already serious builders.

What You'll Do

  • Design and implement new agent workflows with explicit state, task decomposition, tool use, and typed outputs.

  • Build retrieval and citation paths that ground important outputs in source evidence.

  • Add evaluation, tracing, retries, observability, and recovery behavior for multi-step execution.

  • Build the backend services, data models, APIs, and focused product surfaces required to make the workflow useful.

  • Test agent behavior against realistic success cases, failure cases, and incomplete evidence.

  • Work directly with engineers and domain experts, demonstrate progress frequently, and make pragmatic scope decisions.

Requirements

  • Currently pursuing an undergraduate or master's degree in computer science, computer engineering, or a related technical field.

  • Strong programming fundamentals and experience building a substantial software project, developer tool, backend system, or open-source contribution.

  • Hands-on experience building a nontrivial agent, retrieval system, tool-using workflow, evaluation harness, or multi-step automation system.

  • Clear personal ownership of the work: you can explain what you implemented, the decisions you made, and what you would improve.

  • Ability to reason about state, failure modes, grounding, evaluation, and engineering tradeoffs—not only prompts and model selection.

  • High agency and comfort working through ambiguous problems in a fast-moving environment.

  • Ability to work fully in person in Los Altos. Semester or quarter interns must commit at least 20 hours per week; summer interns should be available full time.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with Python, FastAPI, Postgres, agent frameworks, retrieval systems, or vector databases.

  • Backend, distributed-systems, infrastructure, data-pipeline, or end-to-end product experience.

  • Experience with tests, deployment, observability, security, or reliable failure handling.

  • Experience building systems involving citations, provenance, human review, or other high-stakes correctness requirements.

  • Strong open-source work, prior software-engineering internships, or an independently shipped product with real users.

Compensation

$35–$55 per hour. Exact compensation within the range depends on demonstrated expertise, relevant experience, and the time the student can commit.

Location, Relocation & Visa

This role is fully in person in Los Altos, CA. Academic-term interns must be able to work from the office at least 20 hours per week; summer interns should expect a full-time commitment. Relocation assistance may be offered selectively to a strong candidate and is not guaranteed. Candidates of any nationality or visa status may be considered when the internship can be employed legally; candidate-specific work authorization must be confirmed before employment begins.

Interview Process

Semester/quarter route:

  • 30-minute introductory call → one-day onsite in Los Altos → decision.

Summer route:

  • 15-minute introductory call → take-home assignment → take-home interview → interview with Yeongjun → decision.

  • For some summer candidates, the final two interviews may instead be combined into a one-day onsite in Los Altos.

Equal Opportunity & Accommodation

Cheiron is an equal-opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

The Total Rewards Analyst, HR Technology (HRIT) serves as the strategic functional lead for Compensation, Benefits, Payroll readiness, and Total Rewards technology processes within Rheem’s Oracle Fusion HCM ecosystem. This role drives end-to-end ownership of Total Rewards modules — ensuring platform optimization, data integrity, regulatory compliance, and seamless coordination between HR, Finance, and Payroll operations. This position will serve Rheem North America, located in Atlanta, GA (Hybrid). This role follows our hybrid work arrangement, with team members working in the office Monday through Thursday and remotely on Fridays.

  • Lead Compensation and Benefits system governance within Oracle Fusion HCM, establishing configuration standards, process controls, and data integrity frameworks that ensure accurate and compliant total rewards delivery across all Rheem business units and global manufacturing regions.

  • Support payroll integration coordination by managing the functional design, testing, and validation of data flows between Oracle Compensation, Benefits, and Payroll modules — ensuring seamless end-to-end processing for salary changes, bonus payments, benefits deductions, and statutory reporting across North America, LATAM, and APAC.

  • Manage annual compensation cycle technology readiness including merit, bonus, and equity plan configuration in Oracle Compensation — coordinating with HR leadership, Finance, and IT to ensure timely, accurate, and secure execution of enterprise-wide compensation programs across corporate and plant populations.

title: Research Fellow - Immunology - Oh lab
description:
A postdoctoral fellowship position is available immediately in the Department of Immunology at Mayo Clinic in Scottsdale, AZ under the supervision of Dr. SangKon Oh, PhD, a Professor of Immunology of the Mayo Clinic Graduate School of Biomedical Sciences.

The research fellow/senior research fellow will participate to our research program for the induction and maintenance of immune tolerance in the context of transplantation rejection and inflammatory diseases. Individuals will train in the research program of a Mayo Clinic principal investigator. Qualified individuals will demonstrate the potential for research as evidenced by their training and peer-reviewed publications and should become competitive for national research grants. Proof of English proficiency is required for J-1 Short-Term Scholars, Research Scholars, Professors, Specialists, and Student Interns sponsored by Mayo Clinic.

Must have a Ph.D., M.D., or equivalent doctoral degree in a field deemed relevant by the program. Research Fellow is appropriate for individuals who have completed no more than one prior postdoctoral fellowship, at Mayo Clinic or elsewhere.

Qualified candidates should send their NIH formatted biosketch and/or curriculum vitae, a brief statement of interest that includes their qualifications, and contact details of at least three references.

description:
Engineer, Senior – Mechanical and Piping (242071)

About Us

New Porgera Limited (NPL) is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable practices and community engagement in Papua New Guinea. As the operator of the Porgera Gold Mine, we focus on extracting high-quality mineral resources while prioritizing the well-being of our employees, the environment, and the local communities. About the role

NPL is seeking an experienced and motivated Engineer, Senior - Mechanical & Piping to join the Capital & Projects Department. Reporting directly to the Superintendent - Engineering Projects, the Mechanical & Piping Senior Engineer will be responsible for leading mechanical and piping engineering activities associated with project design, engineering reviews, procurement support, contractor management, and project execution.

This role requires a proactive engineering professional capable of managing multiple projects simultaneously, providing technical oversight, mentoring junior engineers, and ensuring engineering deliverables meet company standards, project objectives, and regulatory requirements.

The successful candidate will play a key role in delivering safe, efficient, and cost-effective engineering solutions while supporting project development, procurement activities, construction execution, and operational readiness initiatives.

Key Responsibilities

In this role, you will:

• Prepare and provide inputs to design deliverables but not limited to technical reports, documents and drawings including PIDs, datasheets and Material take-off orders (MTOs), inclusive and flange/gasket/bolting rating and selection.
• Provide work scope packages for engineering specification, design criteria and procurement support for work scope packages at various stages for all projects
• Be able to perform or review pipe stress analysis for critical lines viz., thermal expansion, support spacing, and equipment nozzle loading checks
• Specify right material of construction (metallurgy) and design ratings (pressure/ temperature) in accordance with applicable codes for the required process duty (inclusive corrosion allowance/ erosive/ slurry service etc)
• Build strong collaborative working relationships, manage contractors, consultants and support key stakeholders at various stages to adhere technical and statutory compliance, quality delivery, and ensure schedule baselines and contractual obligations.
• Able to produce technical drawings using AutoCAD software
• Prepare budget plans for Approval for Expenditure (AFE) and ensure projects are executed within the budget limits at appropriate stages
• Design Clear Plans process, materials tools and systems to ensure smooth flow of project transitions
• Perform risk assessments and develop mitigation plans
• Manage and mentor junior engineer(s)
• Maintain a high level of health and safety awareness and comply with NPL Occupational Health & Safety Policy and all health rules and procedures

About You

Qualifications, Skills & Experience

• A bachelor-degree in Mechanical Engineering
• Minimum 8 years' relevant experience in mechanical and piping engineering.
• Strong technical or engineering design background including processing equipment, such as crushers, mills and conveyors
• Proficient with applicable standards such as:
 ASME B31.3 - piping/ flange classes and ratings
 ANSI/ ASME B16.5 - product standards
 AS1210/ ASME section VIII - pressure vessel codes (static equipment)
 AS/NZS 3500 - Plumbing and drainage code
 ASME B16.34 (Valves), or equivalent
• Strong technical knowledge of rotating equipment (API 610/ 618 for pumps/, compressors, fans/blowers) and static equipment (tanks, piping systems).
• Mining or mineral processing experience is desirable.
• Experience in engineering project management.
• Proficiency in AutoCAD; AutoCAD 3D / CAESAR II (stress analysis) / Inventor or Solid works experience is advantageous.
• Proven track record of seamless cross-function coordination and able to function effectively on interdepartmental assignments as required.
• Strong communication, planning, analytical and problem-solving skills
• Excellent communication and stakeholder management abilities.
• Ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively in a dynamic operational environment

Mobilization Requirement

This is a PNG National position, a site-based role on a FIFO arrangement with a rotation of 21 days on and 14 days off. Candidates must successfully pass a pre-employment medical, including drug and alcohol screening (to be arranged only for successful candidates after the interview stage), and provide an up-to-date Police Clearance Certificate (acquired within the last 6 months). Candidates must be PNG Nationals and available to start immediately. Females are encouraged to apply.

Join Our Team as an Engineer, Senior – Mechanical and Piping

Embark on a rewarding career with NPL as an Engineer, Senior – Mechanical and Piping. This role offers a unique opportunity to work with a dynamic team to contribute to NPL’s success. Enjoy a balanced work schedule, competitive compensation, and a chance to develop your career and technical expertise in a supportive and professional environment.

Note: This advert will be open until 14th September 2026. If you do not hear from NPL within next two (2) weeks following the closing date, please consider your application unsuccessful for this opportunity.

Client Leadership

  • Navigate complex client organizations and serve as a confident, solutions-oriented point of escalation when needed.

B2B Strategy

  • Lead the development of integrated B2B strategies spanning brand, demand generation, customer acquisition, account growth, and retention.
  • Apply a deep understanding of long and complex sales cycles, buying committees, category dynamics, and the relationship between marketing and sales.
  • Connect upper-funnel brand investment with lower-funnel demand, pipeline, and revenue objectives.
  • Guide audience, content, channel, and measurement strategies across the full buyer journey.
  • Ensure strategic recommendations reflect the needs of multiple decision-makers and influencers within an account.
  • Turn market, audience, customer, intent, and performance data into clear strategic direction.

Account-Based Marketing

  • Advise clients on the development and evolution of their ABM strategies, including 1, 1, and 1:1 programs.
  • Help clients determine the appropriate balance between broad demand generation and account-based activation.

  • Connect ABM strategy across marketing, media, sales, CRM, content, and technology teams.
  • Evaluate ABM program maturity and establish practical roadmaps that enable clients to scale over time.
  • Ensure ABM programs are grounded in customer value, strong audience intelligence, and clearly defined business outcomes.

B2B Technology and Data

  • Maintain a strong working knowledge of the B2B marketing technology ecosystem, including ABM platforms, intent data, CRM, marketing automation, content syndication, identity and audience solutions, activation platforms, and measurement tools.
  • Understand how platforms such as Demandbase, 6sense, Salesforce, Adobe, HubSpot, LinkedIn, and other B2B data and technology partners contribute to an integrated marketing ecosystem.

New Business and Practice Growth

  • Play a leadership role in new-business opportunities, from initial discovery and strategic development through pitch delivery.

  • Partner with strategy, media, data, analytics, creative, technology, and commercial leaders across Omnicom to build integrated proposals.
  • Lead or contribute to executive-level pitch presentations, workshops, and chemistry meetings.
  • Partner closely with the President of B2B to codify and evolve Omnicom’s B2B methodologies, products, thought leadership, and go-to-market proposition.
  • Identify emerging client needs and market opportunities that can inform new capabilities and commercial offerings.
  • Represent Omnicom’s B2B practice at industry events, client forums, and partner engagements as appropriate.

Omnicom B2B Practice Leadership

  • Support the President of B2B in executing the vision and growth strategy for Omnicom’s B2B practice.
  • Help connect and mobilize B2B capabilities, talent, tools, and expertise from across the Omnicom network.
  • Encourage collaboration across agencies and disciplines to deliver connected, enterprise-level solutions for clients.
  • Contribute to the development of proprietary B2B products, partnerships, research, and thought leadership.
  • Help establish consistent standards for B2B strategy and client delivery across the network.
  • Act as a visible ambassador for Omnicom’s B2B proposition, both internally and externally.

Team Leadership

  • Provide senior direction and mentorship to multidisciplinary client teams.
  • Establish a clear strategic vision while empowering functional leaders to deliver against it.
  • Create alignment across strategy, media, creative, data, analytics, technology, and account leadership.
  • Raise the quality of strategic thinking, client counsel, and executive communication across the practice.
  • Develop talent by coaching team members, creating growth opportunities, and encouraging collaboration.
  • Foster a culture of curiosity, accountability, inclusion, and commercial thinking.

Qualifications

  • Approximately 12–15+ years of experience in B2B marketing, strategy, media, consulting, agency leadership, or a related discipline.
  • Significant experience advising complex B2B organizations and senior client stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead multiple major client relationships simultaneously.
  • Deep understanding of B2B audiences, buying groups, customer journeys, sales cycles, and go-to-market models.
  • Strong knowledge of brand strategy, demand generation, ABM, integrated media, data, technology, and measurement.
  • Working familiarity with leading ABM, CRM, marketing automation, intent-data, and B2B activation platforms.
  • Proven success leading or materially contributing to new-business pitches and organic account growth.
  • Ability to simplify complex business and technology concepts into clear strategic recommendations.
  • Strong executive presence, storytelling ability, and written and verbal communication skills.
  • Experience leading multidisciplinary teams within a matrixed organization.
  • Commercially minded, with the ability to connect marketing strategy to pipeline, revenue, customer growth, and enterprise value.
  • Experience working across a complex agency network or similarly matrixed organization is preferred.

Leadership Attributes

The successful candidate will be:

  • A strategic thinker who can move confidently between enterprise growth challenges and activation details.
  • A trusted advisor who brings a clear point of view while remaining collaborative and pragmatic.
  • A relationship builder who can earn credibility with clients, internal teams, and external partners.
  • A connector who can mobilize talent and capabilities from across the Omnicom network.
  • A translator who connects marketing, sales, media, data, and technology.
  • A modern B2B practitioner who understands that brand and demand must work together.
  • An inspiring leader who raises the ambition and quality of the work.
  • A growth-oriented operator who can identify opportunities and turn them into action.

Measures of Success

Success in this role will be demonstrated through:

  • Strong senior-level relationships and client satisfaction across the assigned portfolio.
  • High-quality, strategically consistent work that advances client business objectives.
  • Client retention and organic revenue growth.
  • Meaningful contributions to new-business wins.
  • Increased adoption and effectiveness of modern B2B and ABM capabilities.
  • Strong integration across client, agency, and partner teams.
  • Effective partnership with the President of B2B and leaders across Omnicom.
  • Development of high-performing talent and future B2B leaders.
  • Continued growth and differentiation of Omnicom’s B2B practice.
