title: Counsel, Energy
description:
About Fluidstack

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it.

We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Legal Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Build the legal and compliance function from zero, for the largest compute buildout in history. No inherited playbook, no legacy team. The systems, standards, and team we build are the ones a company deploying gigawatts will run on for the next decade.

  • Make legal a source of speed. We structure and close complex deals in weeks that typically take quarters. That only work when we calibrate risk from first principles of business enablement. Our job is judgment, applied fast enough that legal helps drive the deal across the finish line.

  • Cover the entire legal surface with a lean team. A small team owns everything, and much of it involves business structures the market hasn’t seen before. You invent the solution with our business team.

Role Scope

  • Structure, draft, and negotiate the energy agreements that power Fluidstack’s data center buildout, including power purchase agreements, interconnection and transmission agreements, on-site and behind-the-meter generation, and utility infrastructure and services agreements.

  • Advise on energy regulatory matters across FERC, state public utility commissions, and organized markets (ERCOT, PJM, MISO, SPP), and shape our engagement with utilities and regulators as we bring gigawatts of load online.

  • Run complex negotiations with sophisticated counterparties end to end, balancing legal risk against the speed our business demands.

  • Manage outside counsel across substantive disciplines with rigor on scope, quality, and spend.

  • Quarterback transactions cross-functionally with energy, site selection, development, and delivery teams so deals never stall.

  • Advise business leaders as a strategic partner, anticipating legal and commercial issues before they arise and having solutions ready.

What We’re Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don’t fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You hold an active license to practice law in at least one jurisdiction and can meet admission requirements where you will practice.

  • You’ve autonomously structured, drafted, and negotiated complex commercial agreements as lead attorney, against sophisticated counterparties, in areas that map directly to powering data centers: power purchase agreements, energy supply and hedging, interconnection and transmission, generation development, utility infrastructure and services agreements, or similar.

  • You’ve personally made sound, commercially pragmatic calls in ambiguous, high-stakes situations, and colleagues can point to deals where your judgment changed the outcome.

  • You’ve overseen outside counsel across multiple disciplines and held them to a rigorous bar on scope, quality, and spend.

  • You write and speak clearly enough to turn a dense legal issue into a decision and a next step for an executive or a counterparty.

  • Bonus: A mix of law firm and in-house experience. Using AI to improve legal work and efficiency. In-house experience at a data center developer, cloud company, utility, or independent power producer.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

title: Extended Learning Education Consultant, Part-Time: Social Work Office of Research & Public Service - UTK
description:
The Extended Learning Education Consultant will work with SWORPS’ project team dedicated to supporting Local Education Agencies (LEAs), Community-Based Organizations (CBOs), Faith-Based Organizations (FBOs) and other entities that serve PK-12 students with grants administered by the Tennessee Department of Education. The project team’s coordinator will serve as the supervisor for this position. A key responsibility for this position is development and management of an appropriate blend of self-assessments, desktop reviews and site visits to ensure program compliance of grantees including analyzing, interpreting data, and identifying areas of concern. This position is externally funded. This position requires in-state travel. This is a part-time position that is expected to work around 30 hours weekly.

This is a grant-funded position and is contingent upon the continued funding of the grant.

  • Serve as subject matter expert on local, state, and federal fiscal policies and procedures for Local Education Agencies (LEAs) and Community Based Organizations (CBOs) that receive the 21st Century Community Learning Centers (CCLC) and Lottery for Education Afterschool Programs (LEAPs) grants and determine compliance with regulations, policies, and procedures.

  • Maintain currency on relevant Tennessee Department of Education guidance, and state and federal policies and procedures.

  • Develop and manage an appropriate blend of self-assessments, desktop reviews and site visits to ensure program compliance of grantees including analyzing, interpreting data, and identifying areas of concern.

  • Provide responsive and timely communication to grantee inquiries.

  • Collaborate with grantees when needed to identify methods of resolution and options for corrective action.

  • Liaison with grantees for project evaluation needs and work with other members of the SWORPS project team on development of policies and procedures to improve data quality.

  • Facilitate or monitor changes resulting from program evaluation recommendations.

  • Act as program evaluation champion reinforcing with grantees notion that evaluation activities are intended to drive continuous quality improvement.

  • Provide technical assistance to grantees on how to use the teacher and parent survey results as well as student participation and outcome data to improve their programs.

  • Coordinate new user training on how to access the Extended Learning Afterschool Program (ELAP) data collection system.

  • Provide input for development of training content and other resources to meet grantee ongoing needs.

Required Qualifications

  • Experience: Minimum 5 years’ work experience in compliance/auditing of federal or state programs
  • Education: Master’s degree in public administration, education, public health, social work or related social science field
  • Knowledge, Skills, Abilities:
    • Knowledge of local, state, and federal fiscal policies and procedures for Local Education Agencies and Community Based Organizations that receive 21st Century Community Learning Centers (CCLC) and Lottery for Education Afterschool Programs (LEAPs) grants.
    • Knowledgeable about best practices for quality extended learning programming.
    • Ability to conduct reviews and analyze information to compose clear, concise, timely, and professionally written reports.
    • Knowledgeable about data collection methods and methods for protecting confidential data.
    • Demonstrated experience of strong observational, analytical, and critical thinking skills to be able to review trends, information, and outcomes and deduce reasons for the results and consider alternative possibilities for conclusions and recommendations.
    • Demonstrated strong communication skills to be able to provide clear and concise written and verbal reports that outline findings and highlight the reasoning behind recommendations.
    • Ability to maintain discretion with confidential information.
    • Ability to prioritize tasks, follow through to complete assignments in a timely and accurate manner.
    • Knowledge of MS Office platforms including Excel and PowerPoint. Ability to work independently and in a team setting.

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis without need now or in the future for sponsorship for employment-based visa status.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience:
    • 5 years’ work experience working in extended learning program service delivery settings.
    • Previous experience in extended learning program service delivery.
  • Knowledge, Skills, Abilities:
    • Demonstrated skill in responding to potentially serious compliance issues and violations, and consulting in negotiating resolutions.

Work Location:

  • This position is fully remote, part-time, expected to work 30 hours per week.

Compensation and Benefits:

  • UT market range: MR11

  • Anticipated hiring range: $60,000

  • Find more information on the UT Market Range structure here

  • Find more information on UT Benefits here

To express interest, please submit an application with the noted below attachments:

  • Resume

The Social Work Office of Research and Public Service (SWORPS) is an applied research center of the University of Tennessee College of Social Work (CSW). We are a dynamic and close-knit interdisciplinary team of individuals with a shared vision of thriving communities with equitable outcomes for all. Clinical Lab Assistant I perform pre-analytical specimen receipt, processing, identification verification and specimen storage. The Clinical Lab Assistant I operates centrifuge and pneumatic tube systems, office equipment, enters information and test orders into the laboratory computer system. Education:

HSG High School Grad or Equivalent

This individual will serve as the primary orchestrator for new customer engagements that require customized manufacturing, fulfillment, compliance, or operational support. Success in this role requires the ability to translate customer and business requirements into executable supply chain strategies while aligning cross-functional technical teams to deliver exceptional outcomes.

Customer Engagement Leadership

  • Serve as the primary Supply Chain Operations lead for new customer engagements with unique technical, manufacturing, or operational requirements.
  • Partner with Business Development, Product Management, Engineering, and Operations teams to assess customer needs and define engagement strategies.
  • Evaluate customer requirements and determine operational readiness, manufacturing capabilities, and supply chain implications.
  • Lead customer-facing discussions related to manufacturing, fulfillment, logistics, compliance, quality, and operational scalability.

Technical Program Management

  • Drive end-to-end program execution from engagement qualification through operational launch and ongoing support.
  • Develop comprehensive program plans, milestones, risk assessments, and execution strategies.
  • Coordinate cross-functional technical teams to ensure alignment on deliverables, timelines, and customer commitments.
  • Establish governance structures, communication plans, and executive-level reporting mechanisms.

Manufacturing & Supply Chain Strategy

  • Assess where products will be manufactured and determine the most effective supply chain strategy to support customer requirements.
  • Evaluate manufacturing site capabilities, capacity, tooling, test requirements, quality systems, and fulfillment models.
  • Partner with factory operations, manufacturing engineering, procurement, logistics, quality, and planning teams to develop scalable solutions.
  • Identify gaps in operational readiness and drive mitigation plans.

  • Organize and lead virtual teams across engineering, manufacturing, planning, sourcing, logistics, quality, and business operations.
  • Facilitate decision-making among technical and business stakeholders while balancing customer commitments, operational constraints, and business objectives.
  • Influence senior leadership and drive alignment across organizations with competing priorities.

Risk Management & Continuous Improvement

  • Identify program risks, supply chain constraints, and operational challenges early in the engagement lifecycle.
  • Develop mitigation strategies and contingency plans to ensure successful customer onboarding and product delivery.
  • Drive process improvements that enhance the organization's ability to support future customer engagements efficiently and predictably.

  • Experience managing customer-facing programs and complex operational engagements.

title: Palvelutyöntekijä
description:
Haluatko työskennellä moniammatillisessa työyhteisössä? Kiinnostaako työ, jossa tehtävät ovat aidosti monipuolisia?

Haemme asiakaspalveluhenkistä ja kehitysmyönteistä palvelutyöntekijää Jorvin sairaalaan toistaiseksi voimassa olevaan työsuhteeseen.

HUSin tukipalvelut, viralliselta nimeltään Runkopalvelut, vastaa siitä, että sairaalassa on parhaat mahdolliset puitteet potilaiden hoitamiseksi.

Palvelutyöntekijänä meillä Jorvissa pääset huolehtimaan monipuolisesti aulapalveluiden ja laitoshuollon tehtävistä.

Aulapalveluiden työtehtäviin kuuluu esimerkiksi asiakaspalvelua ja neuvontaa, potilaiden ilmoittautumisten vastaanottamista, avaintenhallintaa ja löytötavaroiden käsittelyä.

Laitoshuolto sisältää puhtaanapitoa ja ruokahuollon avustavia tehtäviä sekä esimerkiksi vuodehuoltoa, pyykkihuoltoa ja erilaisten tuotetilausten tekoa.

Työpaikan sijainti:Jorvin sairaala, Espoo

Työsuhde:vakituinen, kokoaikainen, 3-vuorotyö (sisältää viikonlopputyötä)

Työehtosopimus ja palkkaus:HYVTES, tehtäväkohtainen palkka on2633,45€/kk + sopimuksen mukaiset lisät

Työn aloitus:syyskuun lopulla tai sopimuksen mukaan

Tutustu palvelutyöntekijämme tarinaan täällä:https://www.hus.fi/ajankohtaista/palvelutyontekijasta-moneksi

Miksi töihin HUSin Runkopalveluihin?
* Monipuolisissa potilaan hoitoa tukevissa tehtävissä olet tärkeä osa sairaalamaailmaa.
* Kattava perehdytys: kukaan ei joudu kylmiltään työntekoon. Saat myös aina apua perehdytyksen jälkeenkin.
* Rento ja monimuotoinen työyhteisö, johon jokaisen työntekijän on helppoa tulla mukaan. Meillä kaikki auttavat toisiaan parhaansa mukaan ja töitä tehdään yhdessä hyvällä fiiliksellä.
* Monipuoliset ura ja koulutusmahdollisuudet.
* Työterveyshuolto, liikunta-, kulttuuri- ja työsuhdematkaetu, tuettu työpaikkaruokailu sekä vaihtuvia henkilökuntaetuja liikunta- ja hyvinvointipalveluista.

Mitä toivomme sinulta?

Ilahdumme hyvistä vuorovaikutustaidoista ja iloisesta palveluasenteesta, sillä teet töitä tiiviisti työkavereidesi kanssa asiakkaidemme hyvinvoinnin eteen. Lisäksi toivomme ammattimaista ja reipasta työotetta, koska työ on vaihtelevaa ja jokainen työpäivä voi olla erilainen. Toivomme, että tietojärjestelmien käyttö on sinulle tuttua ja suhtaudut asioihin positiivisella otteella.

Suomen kielen suullinen ja kirjallinen taito on välttämätön. Tehtävässä tarvitaan hygieniapassi.

Näin haet

Lähetä hakemus sähköisellä hakulomakkeella hakuajan loppuun mennessä. Voimme aloittaa haastattelut jo hakuaikana.

HUSissa olet osa vaikuttavinta hoitoa.

Tehtävän kelpoisuusehdot

Soveltuva toisen asteen ammatillinen koulutus tai soveltuva työkokemus.

Edellytämme asiakas- ja potilastiloissa työskentelevältä tartuntatautilain mukaista rokotussuojaa, ja terveydenhuollon toimintayksiköissä työskentelevältä terveydentilan selvitystä keuhkotuberkuloosista ja salmonellasta.

Tehtävään valittavan tulee olla täysi-ikäinen.

Yhteystiedot

Lisätietoja tehtävästä antaa palveluesihenkilö Merja-Tiina Uitto, p. 050428 4677.

title: Inventory & Order Operations Senior Analyst
location: New York, New York, United States
description:
The Company:

HallPass is building the next generation of candy. Our goal is simple: create the candy people already love, with a fraction of the calories, at the same price. HallPass recently launched nationwide at Walmart.

HallPass is part of the Medici Brands portfolio, alongside brands like David. This is a rare opportunity to join a breakout food brand at a pivotal stage of growth. Led by CEO Peter Rahal, Cofounder and Former CEO of RXBAR, and President Michael Tierney, Founder and Former CEO of Stuffed Puffs, HallPass brings together deep experience building and scaling category-defining consumer brands.

HallPass is working to reimagine one of the largest and most iconic categories in food, proving that better nutrition doesn't have to come at the expense of taste or price. With national distribution and ambitious plans to expand our product portfolio and retail presence, HallPass is working to become a leading candy brand in the U.S. and beyond.


Roles & Responsibilities:

As an inventory and order operations senior analyst, you will own the day-to-day inventory and production transactions in NetSuite, ensuring our systems accurately reflect the physical flow of materials and finished goods across the supply chain.

You’ll work closely with Supply Chain, Operations, Finance, co-manufacturers, and 3PL partners to maintain accurate inventory and resolve discrepancies quickly.

NetSuite & Inventory

  • Be the day-to-day owner of inventory and production transactions in NetSuite.
  • Maintain NetSuite as the source of truth for the flow of goods across our supply chain.
  • Build and maintain Bills of Materials (BOMs), working with Supply Chain leadership for review and approval.
  • Ensure inventory quantities, locations, and movements accurately reflect physical inventory across our network.
  • Identify and resolve inventory discrepancies before they become larger operational or financial issues.


Purchase Orders & Material Flow

Own the system transactions behind the full lifecycle of our materials and finished goods, including:

  • Raw material and packaging purchase orders.
  • Receipt of raw and packaging inventory.
  • Purchase orders to co-manufacturers.
  • Inventory transfers from 3PLs to co-manufacturers.
  • Receipt and movement of finished goods from co-manufacturers back to 3PLs.
  • Finished-goods movements through fulfillment to end customers.


Production & Work Orders

  • Create, maintain, and close production work orders in NetSuite.
  • Ensure materials issued to production are accurately captured.
  • Manage the post-production backflush process for unused raw and packaging materials.
  • Reconcile expected versus actual material consumption after each production run.
  • Produce consumption and variance reporting that helps the team understand co-manufacturer performance, yield, and scrap.
  • Work with Supply Chain to investigate material variances and improve inventory accuracy over time.

Requirements

  • Strong working knowledge of NetSuite, with hands-on experience managing inventory, purchase orders, work orders, inventory transfers, receipts, and production transactions.
  • Experience working with inventory and material flows in a manufacturing, CPG, food & beverage, or similar operational environment.
  • Strong understanding of inventory management and the relationship between physical inventory movements and system transactions.
  • Exceptionally detail-oriented, with a high bar for data accuracy and the ability to identify and resolve discrepancies.
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple transactions, production runs, and priorities simultaneously.
  • A proactive problem-solver with strong follow-through, ownership, and a willingness to dig into issues until they are resolved.
  • Comfortable working cross-functionally with Supply Chain, Operations, Finance, co-manufacturers, and 3PL partners.
  • No ego when it comes to pitching in and doing what is needed to keep operations running smoothly.
  • Collaborative, self-driven, and excited to grow with a fast-moving team.

Benefits

  • This is a full-time, in-office role based in New York City. We work onsite five days a week- when the culture fits, it is fun to be in the office together.
  • Salary: $115,000-$125,000 per year, inclusive of bonus.
  • Company equity options.
  • 100% covered Health, Vision, Dental Insurance.
  • 401(k) with 4% match.
  • Additional perks, such as covered gym expenses.
  • Substantial and required PTO.

title: Asset Intelligence Officer
description:
Are you passionate about turning data into meaningful insight that drives decision making? Do you enjoy solving complex problems and improving processes?

Well this could be for you! We’re looking for an Asset Intelligence Officer to join our growing Strategic Asset Data team and play a key role in shaping how we use data to drive continuous improvement and meet business objectives.

This is an exciting new role within a growing function, meaning you’ll have the opportunity to truly make your mark.

About the role

As an Asset Intelligence Officer, you’ll sit at the heart of our Strategic Asset Data team, supporting how we collect, manage, analyse and use data across multiple systems.

Your work will directly support investment planning, compliance, and service delivery, ensuring decisions are based on reliable, high-quality information. You’ll combine data analysis, business analysis, and process improvement, helping us improve how data flows across teams and systems.

You’ll work with a wide range of stakeholders across property investment and asset management, helping them move away from time-consuming data tasks so they can focus on delivering better outcomes.

If you enjoy variety, collaboration and the chance to influence change, this role offers genuine scope to grow and develop.

Some of the key duties in the role are:

Analysing asset data to identify trends, issues and opportunities for improvement

Producing reports, dashboards and insights using tools like Excel and Power BI

Mapping current (“as-is”) processes and helping design improved (“to-be”) solutions

Working closely with stakeholders to understand data needs and deliver solutions

Supporting the integration and consistency of data across systems

About you

You’ll bring with you experience of working in asset management or social housing to help set you up for success, that foundation is key for this role. Alongside this, you’ll have experience working in a data or an analytical role.

You’ll need to be able to demonstrate strong excel skills and ideally would have had used tools such as Power BI, SharePoint or SQL although this isn’t essential, it would just be handy for you to have.

As you’ll be working across the teams, communication is key and you’ll need to be able to translate complex data challenges into practical solutions moving forwards meeting the needs of the customer. You’ll need to be able to adapt your communication style and change techy language into something easy to understand for non-technical audiences.

We work flexibly; you’ll do the majority of your work from home but will be willing and able to travel across our operating areas as needed. We currently have hubs in London, Andover, Devizes, Plymouth and access to lots of third party shared workspaces.

What’s in it for me

We invest in our colleagues because we know if they have a better day at work, the service our customers receive will be better. The Aster Offer is our offer to our colleagues to ensure they have a great day at work and includes things like:

Flexible working – whilst some roles need to be carried out in a specific place at a specific time, where possible we encourage our colleagues to work to their own schedule at a location that suits them, their team and our business’ needs

A focus on colleague wellbeing – workshops, an employee assistance programme offering counselling and support, mental health training and a health cash plan

We invest in colleagues’ careers and development through our leader and colleague development frameworks

Defined Contribution Pension and attached life assurance

Volunteering hours available to all colleagues to enable them to give back

Savings at cinemas, gyms, holidays, days out, various shops and eateries and lots more

Enhanced leave

We celebrate colleagues who go above and beyond with a range of personalised recognition initiatives

Ready to apply?

To apply, please use information provided in the advert and role profile to let us know why you’d be good for the job. Please submit a copy of your up-to-date CV along with a supporting statement.

We create an inclusive workplace that promotes and values diversity and believe that creating an environment where everyone, from any background, can do their best work is the right thing to do.

All candidates will be required to verify their right to work in the UK prior to commencement of employment with the Aster Group & it’s subsidiary brands.

This position provides dedicated afternoon and evening operational coverage and is regularly scheduled Monday through Friday, 2:00 PM–10:00 PM Eastern Time. title: Senior Forward Deployed Engineer
description:
Position: Senior Forward Deployed Engineer

Location: London or Amsterdam, 3 days a week in office

The Role:

We're looking for a technically sharp, product-minded engineer to help push the frontier of AI across Just Eat Takeaway. You'll work with some of our most ambitious internal teams and technology partners - helping them get the most out of advanced AI, and turning those learnings into durable improvements across our organisation.

This is a builder role. You'll dig into complex workflows, identify the gaps that matter, and translate them into concrete technical insights that shape how we build. If you're as comfortable debugging a live workflow as you are designing an evaluation framework or presenting findings to a non-technical audience, you'll fit right in.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Work directly with internal teams and strategic partners to understand critical workflows, uncover failure modes, and identify the highest-impact opportunities for AI improvement.

  • Prototype and iterate on prompts, agents, and workflow designs to understand system behaviour and unlock real value - not just theoretical improvements.

  • Synthesise findings for our Product Engineering and Platform teams, turning real usage patterns into clear, reproducible evaluations, benchmarks, and technical artefacts that improve product and platform quality.

  • Build repeatable tools, patterns, and evaluation approaches that raise the quality bar across multiple use cases - not just one-off fixes.

  • Operate with strong judgment in ambiguous environments, balancing immediate technical problem-solving with longer-term systemic improvement.

  • Build relationships across our engineering and product communities, serving as a trusted technical partner to individuals and teams alike.

These are some of the key components to the position:

You'll thrive here if you have strong software engineering and AI fundamentals - whether that's from experience in a startup, or a product focused role in a larger org. Software engineer, ML engineer, data scientist, or equivalent. Product Managers, BAs or Technical Programme Managers keen to return to a builder role. A track record of shipping production systems end-to-end is a strong plus.

What will you bring to the team?

  • Experience building AI applications, agents, or evaluation systems, with the ability to reason clearly about model behaviour in complex workflows.

  • Comfort working directly with highly experienced functional SMEs and translating their challenges into concrete technical signals.

  • Fluency moving between prototyping, debugging, evaluation design, and cross-functional collaboration - sometimes all in the same day.

  • Working across every layer of the stack - Able to switch between configuring a connector in an admin panel to prompting an agent to contribute code back to our underlying platform.

  • Clear communication across technical and non-technical audiences - you can explain what you found and why it matters.

  • High agency and a strong product sense, with a bias toward building things that last rather than one-off fixes.

  • AI First problem solving, deeply experienced with AI tools to drive fast solution creation, able to balance model usage to maximise ROI, everything from coding to design and more.

  • Bonus: Familiarity with complex market place businesses. Experience as an early-stage startup engineer or in a previous FDE style role. None of these is a dealbreaker - we're more interested in how you think than what you've already shipped.

At JET, this is how we play

Our teams forge connections internally and work with some of the best-known brands on the planet, giving us truly international impact in a dynamic environment.

Being the best at what we do isn’t just about delivering on our strategy. It's a competition for something incredibly valuable – our customers' choice. Every time a customer decides where to order, they're picking a side.

At the heart of the JET Customer League are our values and behaviours. They guide every interaction, every decision, every innovation. These are the actions we need to perform consistently and brilliantly, to surpass the competition and earn our customers’ loyalty, again and again.

Fun, fast-paced and supportive, the JET culture is about movement, growth, helping one another to succeed and celebrating wins. By truly living our values and embodying our behaviours, we’re building a customer-first culture which enables us to stay one step ahead of the competition.

Inclusion, Diversity & Belonging

No matter who you are, what you look like, who you love, or where you are from, you can find your place at Just Eat Takeaway.com. We’re committed to creating an inclusive culture, encouraging diversity of people and thinking, in which all employees feel they truly belong and can bring their most colourful selves to work every day.

What else is cooking?

Want to know more about our JETers, culture or company? Have a look at our career site where you can find people's stories, blogs, podcasts and more JET morsels.

description:

Day - 08 Hour (United States of America)

This is a Stanford Health Care job.

The Director of HR Compliance has broad oversight within a business unit including identification, development, progress tracking and outcome reporting. In addition to any newly identified programs, standard required programs are: Quality and Compliance, SHC HR policies and practices remain in compliance with Municipal, County, State and Federal laws. Provides leadership and direction in the development, maintenance and enhancements of the SHC HR polices to meet the needs of SHC Human Resource and client departments. Leads the operational plans for wage/hour compliance. Provides leadership, consultation, and education regarding integration of compliance with regulatory standards across HR programs and operations. Recommends to SHC Human Resource and client departments continuous quality improvement initiatives to maintain continuous hospital accreditation and certification from The Joint Commission, California Department of Health, and other regulatory agencies.

Locations
Stanford Health Care

What you will do

  • The Director of HR Compliance is responsible for ensuring that SHC HR policies and practices are in compliance with Municipal, County, State and Federal laws.

  • The Director of HR Compliance provides direction to activities related to the assessment of compliance with CDPH, CMS and The Joint Commission accreditation standards for the hospital, service lines, and laboratory programs, and their related accreditation process requirements and survey activities.

  • Serves as HR Accreditation Lead with surveyors on audits and investigations of our employee HR records and provide timely submission of proof on elements of compliance.

  • Develops strategic plans and leads improvement to mitigate the potential of HR-related risks affecting Stanford Health Care’s reputation, security, safety, and sustainability of patient care.

  • Stays abreast of all municipal, county, state and federal labor law changes each year and develops plans to assess if changes to policies, processes and procedures are needed to ensure adapted timely.

  • Liaison to risk management to develop and execute remediation plans identified based on trends of grievances and legal claims to proactively mitigate risk to the organization. Works with legal and across HR as needed to operationalize the plans with the business.

  • Manages the Alternative Work Schedule program to ensure compliance.

  • Develops, enforces, and audits timekeeping policies to ensure accurate tracking of hours worked, meal periods, and rest breaks. Works with Employee Relations team to operationalize findings within each business area.

  • Delivers and supports HR compliance and policy standards to hospital and ambulatory and operational leaders; works with HR leaders as appropriate to develop an effective HR compliance and policy training program as needed.

  • Creates, maintains and oversees document flow of the HR policy approval process.

  • Manages and trains staff on HR compliance components for hospital and service line surveys and audit readiness.

  • Leads recruiting and onboarding to ensure adequate staffing levels to support daily operations.

  • Conducts regular compliance audits of HR policies, procedures, and employee data as needed.


Education Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in a work-related discipline/field from an accredited college or university required.


Experience Qualifications

  • Fifteen (15) years of progressively responsible and directly related work experience, including seven (7) years of management responsibility required.


Required Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Strong hospital management experience, with progressive and in-depth expertise in regulatory compliance. Demonstrated understanding of applicable regulations and regulatory agencies.

  • Ability to analyze, organize, and problem solve, with ability to identify system vulnerabilities and develop and apply innovative solutions.

  • Ability to direct and manage the development and implementation of projects and processes for high impact programs and communications.

  • Ability to foster effective working relationships and build consensus.

  • Ability to identify, design and administer plans that support hospital strategic goals and attract, reward and retain talent.

  • Ability to mediate and resolve complex problems and issues.

  • Ability to provide leadership and influence others.

  • Knowledge of HR functional operations, business systems and processes.

  • Knowledge of local, state and federal regulatory requirements related to areas of functional responsibility and HR.

  • Knowledge of principles and practices of organization, administration, fiscal and personnel management.

  • Knowledge and experience with federal (?) and State of California wage and hour compliance.


Licenses and Certifications

  • Advanced professional certifications such as SHRM-SCP, SPHR, or specialized compliance certifications are preferred.

Full time 37.5 hours

We make health happen

At Bupa, our purpose is simple: helping people live longer, healthier, happier lives and making a better world.

As a Technology Delivery Lead, you'll play a key role in making that happen. You'll lead the technology delivery of mergers and acquisitions within our Diagnostics and Secondary Care business, helping newly acquired healthcare organisations successfully integrate into Bupa.

This is an opportunity to lead complex, high-profile programmes that directly support the growth of our healthcare services. You'll work across technology, change and business teams to deliver technology solutions that create value for colleagues, clinicians and customers. From shaping delivery roadmaps to ensuring successful implementation and business readiness, you'll have end-to-end ownership of initiatives that have a real impact on healthcare delivery.

We're looking for someone who enjoys bringing people together, navigating complexity and creating clarity. You'll lead through collaboration, helping teams deliver great outcomes while fostering a culture of continuous improvement, innovation and shared success.

How you’ll help us make health happen:

  • Lead the end-to-end delivery of technology workstreams supporting mergers and acquisitions across Health Services.

  • Oversee the integration of technology services, platforms and capabilities into Bupa following acquisitions.

  • Create and manage delivery plans, roadmaps and priorities, ensuring alignment with business objectives.

  • Work closely with Product Owners, business stakeholders and delivery teams to maintain a clear and prioritised backlog.

  • Coordinate multiple teams, dependencies and delivery partners to achieve successful outcomes.

  • Identify, manage and communicate risks, issues and dependencies, taking action to keep delivery on track.

  • Provide clear and transparent reporting on progress, budget, forecasts and key delivery metrics.

  • Build strong relationships across technology, operational and business teams.

  • Lead and coach teams through Agile ways of working, encouraging collaboration, accountability and continuous improvement.

  • Champion Agile practices including sprint planning, retrospectives, reviews and programme increment planning.

  • Support business case development and benefits tracking to make sure value is delivered and realised.

  • Ensure delivery activities align with governance, regulatory and data protection requirements.

  • Manage relationships with third-party suppliers and delivery partners to achieve shared goals.

Key Skills / Qualifications needed for this role:

We're looking for an experienced technology delivery professional who can successfully lead large-scale programmes in complex environments.

You'll bring:

  • Significant experience delivering complex IT projects and programmes using Agile, Waterfall and hybrid methodologies.

  • Experience leading multi-stream technology initiatives with multiple stakeholders and dependencies.

  • Strong knowledge of Agile frameworks, including Scrum and SAFe.

  • Experience delivering technology integration, transformation or mergers and acquisitions programmes.

  • Excellent stakeholder management skills with the ability to engage and influence senior leaders.

  • Strong commercial awareness, including budget management, forecasting and supplier management.

  • Experience managing risks, issues, dependencies and competing priorities.

  • The ability to lead, coach and inspire cross-functional teams.

  • Strong communication skills with the ability to translate technical information for different audiences.

  • Experience working with distributed teams and external delivery partners.

  • A good understanding of enterprise technology platforms, systems and integration approaches.

Desirable qualifications:

  • PRINCE2

  • PMP

  • SAFe Agilist

  • Certified ScrumMaster (CSM)

  • AgilePM or equivalent delivery certifications

Benefits

Our benefits are designed to make health happen for our people. Viva is our global wellbeing programme and includes all aspects of our health – from mental and physical, to financial, social and environmental wellbeing. We support flexible working and have a range of family friendly benefits.


Joining Bupa in this role you will receive the following benefits and more:

  • Annual leave entitlement of 25 days + bank holidays increasing with length of service

  • In-house training for all staff

  • Company pension scheme

  • Life assurance

  • Employee Referral Scheme

  • Access to subsidised staff restaurant

Why Bupa?

We're a health insurer and provider. With no shareholders, our customers are our focus. Our people are all driven by the same purpose – helping people live longer, healthier, happier lives and making a better world. We make health happen by being brave, caring and responsible in everything we do.


We encourage all of our people to "Be you at Bupa". We champion diversity and understand the importance of our people representing the communities and customers we serve. That's why we especially encourage applications from people with diverse backgrounds and experiences.


Bupa is a Level 2 Disability Confident Employer. This means we aim to offer an interview/assessment to every disabled applicant who meets the minimum criteria for the role. title: Technical Product Manager - AI Finance App
description:
About KIRA

Our mission is to make money smart, reliable and within reach for everyone.

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it's the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in Asia and it includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and at ease and self reliance, become an expert. We believe AI will help us achieve this in our generation.

We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.

What You'll Own

  • Own a vertical end-to-end - outcomes and metrics, a backlog prioritised by value / risk / dependency / strategic priority, acceptance criteria crisp enough to build and test against.

  • Shape the technical design with engineering - system boundaries, money-movement correctness (idempotency, ledgering, reconciliation), third-party-rail reliance and rail-down behaviour, failure/retry/refund paths, security, latency, scalability, recovery.

  • Make hard trade-offs across correctness, speed, cost, reliability and UX - and defend them to an engineering, compliance or ops lead who pushes back.

  • Treat regulated constraints as first-class product inputs - licensing scope, CDD/KYC and limits, sanctions/PEP screening, transaction monitoring, data residency and privacy. Know which are hard launch gates and which are forward-readiness.

  • Apply AI where it earns its place - define what it's allowed to decide, where a human stays in the loop, how it's evaluated, and what it does when unsure. Every AI-surfaced number traces back to a real record.

  • Ship against external gates - build feature-complete behind flags; go live per rail as each partner and regulatory gate clears.

  • Work across Engineering, Design, Compliance, Operations, Treasury and Finance/Reconciliation

What We're Looking For

  • Product leadership - significant experience owning a complex technical product end-to-end; strong judgement and decisiveness under ambiguity; ability to balance ambition against technical, regulatory and operational reality; can hold their own with senior engineers.

  • Technical foundation - solid system design (boundaries, datastores, queues/workflows, APIs, failure modes, consistency under concurrency); comfort reading, reviewing and challenging design docs; can sketch an architecture and a sequence. No production code, but technical enough that engineers don't have to simplify.

  • Domain - experience in a regulated / high-consequence domain (payments, banking, remittance, insurance, …) or demonstrable fast-ramp ability; understands why money movement is different (correctness over convenience, irreversible states, partners you don't control).

  • AI judgement - hands-on with LLM-based products; can frame a feature as eval-able (offline, online, human feedback); realistic on hallucination/drift/data gaps, including data-blocked vs model-blocked and when a model must not be in the loop at all.

  • Nice to have - engineer or highly-technical-PM background · zero-to-one · shipped AI-heavy consumer products · defined eval metrics for ML/LLM systems · AI UX + failure-handling intuition · SEA market experience.

Outcome

  • Clear vertical strategy and legible roadmap

  • Ships fast and clears the gates that actually block launch

  • Money is correct and users are never misled about the state of their funds

  • AI features are valuable, predictable and trusted

  • Trade-offs made deliberately under uncertainty and hold up when challenged

  • Engineering, design, compliance, and operations are aligned with minimal friction

Location

This is a remote role. We hire globally and work across multiple countries and time zones.

Candidates should be comfortable working effectively in a distributed, fast-moving international team and collaborating with colleagues across different locations.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Technical interview

  3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

  • Good understanding of secure software delivery and DevSecOps, including CI/CD security, secrets management, and threat modelling.
  • Experience with incident response, including tabletop exercises, playbooks, and coordination of technical and business communications.

  • Work within a community-based practice that supports independence, wellness, and longevity

  • A culture that invests in your growth and values clinician-driven decision-making

​

Employment Types Available

FOX offers multiple pathways to match your lifestyle and career goals:

  • Full-time Speech Language Pathologist – In-Home & Senior Living Care (salaried with benefits)

  • Part-time Speech Language Pathologist – In-Home & Senior Living Care (salaried with benefits eligibility based on minimum hours requirement)

  • Professional certification reimbursement

  • Clinical and nonclinical career advancement pathways

  • Access to advanced technology and tools (including virtual care resources)

  • Valid Speech Language Pathology license in the state(s) of practice, or eligibility to obtain

  • Degree from an accredited Speech Language Pathology program

  • Basic computer and EMR proficiency

  • Current CPR certification

  • Current Certificate of Clinical Competence (ASHA CCC)

Physical Requirements

FOX clinicians must be able to meet the physical demands of in-home and community-based care, including:

  • Exerting medium physical effort, including lifting 25–50 lbs occasionally, 10–25 lbs frequently, and up to 10 lbs constantly

  • Performing CPR

  • Providing moderate to maximum assistance with patient transfers and bed mobility

  • Repositioning patients, standing/walking for extended periods, climbing stairs, and performing therapeutic activities

  • Driving to patient homes and senior living communities as part of the Geriatric House Calls™ model

title: Senior Healthcare Billing Specialist
description:
The Senior Healthcare Billing Specialist is responsible for processing claims for skilled nursing services rendered to residents with third party coverage under Medicare, private insurance, Medicaid, and various co-insurance companies. This role mentors Healthcare Billing Specialists and assigned special projects.

Experience is Everything.

At LCS, experience is everything. We provide you the opportunity to use your talents in a progressive, growing organization that makes a positive difference in the lives of the seniors we serve. If you are seeking an organization that gives back, you’ll love working here. Our principles and hospitality promises define our company culture. LCS employees can be found participating in volunteer activities, getting involved in our committees or collaborating with team members in our innovative workspace. You’ll find several opportunities to grow as a professional, serve the community, and enhance the lives of seniors.

What You’ll Do:

  • Assists with audit preparation.

  • Ensures compliance with current federal and state government regulations for all billing functions.

What We’re Looking For:

  • Prefer minimum of 5 years of experience with healthcare billing, including Medicare, Medicaid and third-party insurance using the UB04 claim format.

  • Proficient with Microsoft Word and Excel

  • Extensive and current working knowledge of various insurance carriers’ payment regulations including various reimbursement schemes, coinsurance and deductibles, and contractual adjustments.
  • Working knowledge of HIPAA regulations and compliance.

Competitive pay, great benefits and vacation time. We are an equal opportunity employer with benefits including medical, dental, life insurance, disability, 401(K) with company match and paid parental leave.

Our Commitment

LCS creates living experiences that enhance the lives of seniors. You’ll see this commitment in our people. They’re talented, dedicated professionals who truly care about residents, with each conducting his or her work with integrity, honesty and transparency according to the principles of LCS. We strive to help every community succeed—strengthening available resources, establishing proven practices that lead to long-term growth and value for those living in, working for and affiliated with the community. title: Business Analyst
description:
Business Analyst

***This position requires an ability to obtain and maintain an active Secret clearance. ***

The Business Analyst supports operations by enabling day-to-day mission operations, production planning and supply chain execution, system and knowledge management, technical writing, and comprehensive metric reporting. This role serves as a core operational enabler by ensuring accurate tracking of deliverables, maintaining organized collaborative environments, and providing actionable analysis that improves operational efficiency, material flow, and leadership decision-making.

Compensation & Benefits:

Estimated Starting Salary Range for Business Analyst: $30hr

Pay commensurate with experience.

Full time benefits include Medical, Dental, Vision, 401K, and other possible benefits as provided. Benefits are subject to change with or without notice.

Business Analyst Responsibilities Include:

  • Provide day-to-day administrative and operational support to ensure seamless mission execution and coordination.
  • Manage and schedule meetings, including coordinating logistics, drafting agendas, capturing official minutes, and tracking action items to closure.
  • Organize, manage, and maintain content within Microsoft SharePoint and Microsoft Teams to ensure accurate record-keeping, version control, and accessible collaboration spaces.
  • Develop and maintain production schedules to ensure timely availability of materials and resources.
  • Monitor production performance metrics and identify trends, risks, inefficiencies, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Support coordination of production activities across departments and teams to maintain alignment and execution tempo.
  • Analyze and track supply chain performance metrics to identify risks, inefficiencies, and improvement opportunities; support on-time delivery and inventory optimization.
  • Collaborate with vendors, suppliers, and internal stakeholders to address supply chain challenges and improve outcomes.
  • Track inventory levels, forecast demand, and develop strategies to maintain appropriate stock levels.
  • Analyze excess and obsolete inventory and provide recommendations for disposition.
  • Support annual and wall-to-wall inventory efforts to improve accuracy and accountability.
  • Assist in the development, management, and continuous update of operational dashboards; build and maintain metric visuals (charts, graphs, status boards) to support leadership decision-making.
  • Track, analyze, and report deliverable metrics and key performance indicators (KPIs) associated with ongoing operations.
  • Develop and deliver recurring and ad-hoc briefings to leadership and stakeholders regarding operational status, deliverables, constraints, and metric performance.
  • Provide technical writing support to draft, review, edit, and format operational documentation, memos, SOPs, and formal reports.
  • Utilize tools such as Excel, ERP/MRP systems, Microsoft applications, Adobe, and databases to conduct analysis and generate reports and visuals.
  • Identify and recommend improvements to streamline operational, production, and supply chain processes.
  • Lead and support continuous improvement initiatives, including CPI efforts and Lean/Six Sigma projects, as applicable.
  • Act as a liaison between operations, production, procurement, and warehouse teams to ensure priorities, deliverables, and constraints are clearly communicated and managed.
  • Assist with program reviews and provide input on material availability, production constraints, capacity planning, and operational readiness.
  • Provide executive support services and contribute to strategic business planning activities as required.
  • Performs other job-related duties as assigned

Business Analyst Experience, Education, Skills, Abilities requested:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Production Planning, Logistics, or related field.
  • 3+ years of experience in business analysis, operations support, production planning, supply chain management, program analysis, or similar roles.
  • Demonstrated excellence in organizational, computer, and record-keeping skills, with strong attention to detail and follow-through.
  • Proven knowledge and practical understanding of data analysis, metric reporting methodologies, and creation of metric visuals and dashboards.
  • Strong proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (especially Excel); expert-level capability with Microsoft tools and related programs (to include SharePoint, Teams) and Adobe.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to effectively brief personnel at varying levels of leadership and produce clear, accurate technical documentation.
  • Strong proficiency in ERP/MRP systems; familiarity with inventory control methods and production scheduling best practices.
  • Analytical mindset with strong problem-solving skills and the ability to translate data into operational decisions.
  • Expert knowledge of CPI processes, strategic business planning, and executive support services.
  • Experience working in warehouse, manufacturing, or military logistics environments preferred.
  • Knowledge of government contracting and compliance requirements preferred.
  • Must pass pre-employment qualifications of Cherokee Federal

Company Information:

Cherokee Nation Government Solutions (CNGS) is a part of Cherokee Federal – the division of tribally owned federal contracting companies owned by Cherokee Nation Businesses. As a trusted partner for more than 60 federal clients, Cherokee Federal LLCs are focused on building a brighter future, solving complex challenges, and serving the government’s mission with compassion and heart. title: Director-Phase 1 Pre-Clerkship Curriculum
description:
General Summary

Under the direction of the Assistant Dean for Undergraduate Medical Education (UME), the Phase 1 Director (Pre-Clerkship Curriculum) – Medical School Campus functions within the Temple University Lewis Katz School of Medicine at WellSpan Health. The Phase 1 Director assists the campus Associate Dean, and the Assistant Dean for UME by directing and implementing the medical school curriculum and scholarly activity for campus students and faculty, including Liaison Committee for Medical Education (LCME) accreditation activities and requirements, student and faculty surveys, and ensuring that the Phase 1 academic curriculum is up-to-date, and effective. This is a WellSpan Health role primarily functioning to support the Temple University Lewis Katz School of Medicine at WellSpan Health campus and students.

Duties and Responsibilities

Essential Functions:

  • Nurtures and fosters relationships with the Temple University Lewis Katz School of Medicine Senior Associate Dean for Medical Education and Associate Dean of Curriculum.
  • Builds and nurtures relationships between Course Directors, Deans, faculty, staff, and students.
  • Leads site Course Director meetings.
  • Mentors Course Directors in giving feedback to students, writing Narrative Summaries, and integrating simulation and evidence-based medicine (EBM) into courses.
  • In collaboration with Student Affairs, serves as a general and specialty-specific career advisor to students and serves as faculty advisor to relevant student organizations.
  • Mentors and advises students in their pre-clerkship education to include remediation, curriculum concerns and their success through United States Medical Licensing Exam (USMLE) Step 1.
  • Participates in M4 (Medical Student 4th Year) Capstone/Transition to Residency course.
  • Participates in M1 (Medical Student 1st Year) Orientation/Transition to Medical School course.
  • Serves on school committees as requested, including, but not limited to, the Admissions Committee, Curriculum Committee, and other committees as needed.
  • Oversees and directs curriculum coordinators.

Common Expectations:

  • Expected to support and meet the values and standards of the organization and the performance expectations of the job, the medical school campus, the department, and the Liaison Committee on Medical Education (LCME) accreditation program.
  • Adherence to all relevant Temple University, local, state, federal, and other student privacy and record-keeping requirements is also expected.

Travel Requirements:

  • Estimated Amount: 5% - Periodic single-day travel to the main campus of the Temple University Lewis Katz School of Medicine in North Philadelphia, Pennsylvania; and/or the Temple/St. Luke’s Regional Medical Campus in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania may be required for several days each year. Overnight travel to regional and/or national Association of American Medical Colleges (AAMC) and/or other similar conferences related to Medical Education and Liaison Committee on Medical Education (LCME) accreditation processes and requirements.

Qualifications

Minimum Education:

  • Doctorate In a field deemed relevant to Medical Education. Required or
  • Doctorate of Philosophy (Ph.D.) In a field deemed relevant to Medical Education. Required

Work Experience:

  • 5 years Prior experience in a medical school campus or other Medical Education setting. Related to education and evaluation of medical students, curriculum design, and/or instructional development and methods. Required

Courses and Training:

  • Receives a faculty appointment, at the appropriate rank, at the Temple University Lewis Katz School of Medicine. within 120 days Required
  • Completes appropriate faculty development activities, courses, seminars, and/or other sessions, as required to maintain faculty appointment at the Temple University Lewis Katz School of Medicine within 1 year and annually thereafter. within 1 year Required

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Current foundational skills and information related to Phase 1 (Pre-clerkship/foundational science) training of medical students, current trends in instructional design and delivery, and fundamental knowledge of Liaison Committee on Medical Education (LCME) medical school accreditation requirements.
  • Develop, lead, and implement a Phase 1 curriculum, in conjunction with leaders at the Temple University North Philadelphia Campus and the St. Luke’s/Bethlehem, Pennsylvania Campus, for medical students at the WellSpan Health campus in York, Pennsylvania.
  • Ability to lead and supervise faculty and staff members participating in developing and delivering the Phase 1 curriculum at the WellSpan Health campus.

Benefits Offered:

  • Comprehensive health benefits
  • Retirement savings plan
  • Paid time off (PTO)
  • Education assistance
  • Financial education and support, including DailyPay
  • Expanded Paid Parental Leave

title: Senior Community Director II
description:
About Prime: Prime Residential is a leading multifamily owner and operator headquartered in San Francisco, with a portfolio of more than 21,000 apartment homes across the West Coast. For more than three decades, we've been committed to caring for communities where residents love to live - pairing well-maintained homes with exceptional service and sought-after locations. We're proud to maintain a richly diverse and inclusive culture where our team members feels welcomed, valued, and set up to do their best work.


Property Details: Coral Bay has a total of 946 units and is located in San Diego, CA.


Schedule: Monday through Friday 9:00 am to 6:00pm


Target Pay: $110,630 per year + performance bonus eligibility


Role Overview: Prime Residential’s Senior Community Directors have full responsibility for maximizing the long-term operating performance of two or more properties, or a single asset with a substantial unit count. In this role, Senior Community Directors drive exceptional talent management and development, excellence in resident and prospect experience based on their thorough understanding of the competitive market, management of financials, maximizing asset financial performance, and upholding policies and procedures to ensure operational excellence for all facets of onsite property management operations (i.e. people, product, promotion and price). This role is viewed as the onsite operations lead across all facets of a community and will effectively and efficiently make sound business decisions in a dynamic and ever-changing multifamily business environment. The role is part of a company-wide team of Community Directors and Senior Community Directors across regions and states, and as such becomes a creator and adaptor of best practices and ensures operating procedures stay consistent and uniform in adherence to other Prime Residential standards. The role will proactively make decisions to ensure stability and adherence to standards of excellence, financial success of the communities, while at the same time, enthusiastically hiring and developing a talented team to contribute to upholding the standards of excellence expected of our communities and associates.


Who You Are:

  • A passionate and unwavering pursuer of excellence
  • Excellent leadership, communication, problem-solving and motivational skills, and a solid business and financial acumen.
  • A disciplined, customer-focused, and financially minded leader, consensus builder and mentor with a very strong eye for talent
  • A passionate individual who can strategize and problem-solve objectively
  • An organized multi-tasker who strives to outperform and exceed expectations, and thrives in a dynamic environment
  • A nimble and flexible leader who can pivot on a moment’s notice as necessitated when duties and responsibilities change without advance notice
  • An exceptional communicator who is comfortable presenting to internal and external stakeholders at all levels
  • A motivated thinker and trainer always striving to recruit top talent with an unrelenting commitment to also grooming and retaining our talent
  • An enthusiastic and personable individual who enjoys building and maintaining relationships
  • A creative coach who inspires top performance out of others
  • A perpetual thinker and firm believer in process improvement
  • A goal-focused leader with the desire to learn, teach and who is not afraid to step out of the box
  • A tech savvy professional not afraid of routine work, and change
  • A diligent and determined associate looking to grow their career in property management

Key Responsibilities:

Talent Management

  • Recruit, engage and retain a team of exceptional property management professionals in office and maintenance positions for communities in scope
  • Embrace and build a team culture focusing on diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging
  • Train newly hired associates on essential job duties utilizing shadowing, role-playing and formalized training processes and techniques
  • Hold regular staff and individual meetings with associates to build relationships and engagement
  • Hold all team members accountable by coaching and providing positive reinforcement and constructive feedback for tenured associates
  • Support and develop the Assistant Managers and Service Managers in their role of managing associates at the site level and in developing a thorough understanding of our business
  • Follow prompt and proper protocols in documenting employee issues, and managing risk
  • Work closely with the Legal and Risk Management team to resolve resident issues and/or necessary remedies to resident homes as peril/loss incidents arise
  • Work closely with Human Resources when counseling and addressing issues requiring progressive discipline, terminations, work-related injuries, or employee-related claims

Competitive Market Position

  • Execute on prescribed marketing plans and maintain curb appeal and advertising focus, while continually evaluating cost per lease and traffic generating strategies
  • Ensure that all associates understand the competitive environment in which we operate
  • Proactively anticipate market changes and be resilient to making prompt and strategic adjustments
  • Know your market and your closest competitors -- your direct manager counts on you to make short, and long-term recommendations for change
  • Proactively make recommendations for any necessary adjustments to market rents and continually seek opportunities for revenue growth
  • Review weekly update reports and develop goals and strategies to address occupancy, future exposure, or high renewals
  • Maintain a comprehensive understanding of the properties’ competitive environment; develop relationships with peers, vendors; and continually update the market survey to adjust operating strategies

Financial Performance

  • Under guidance of direct manager, and with input from Service Managers and Asset Management and Construction team leaders, establish and prepare comprehensive operating budgets for the properties
  • Recommend revenue enhancing capital improvements to manage
  • Monitor properties’ performance relative to budget and be nimble with change
  • Anticipate and communicate budget variances immediately to direct manager
  • Refine revenue and operating expense forecasts for the communities as directed by direct manager

Physical Condition

  • Good communication skills for explaining pricing insights to both technical and non-technical audiences

It provides dedicated program-management leadership for critical, high-risk sites, rapidly removing blockers and maintaining execution momentum during builds and deployments. The role coordinates cross-functional teams to accelerate issue resolution and reduce delays caused by dependencies, unclear ownership, or competing priorities. Without this role, critical deployments face increased risk of late issue discovery, longer site-level escalations, avoidable schedule slips, and reduced predictability in delivery commitments.

Key Responsibilities

  • Identify execution risks across deployment schedules, site readiness, validation, supply chain, operations, and inter-team dependencies; establish and drive mitigation plans 6–8 weeks before potential impact.

  • Lead rapid-response execution for critical deployments and high-risk sites, including escalation management, decision tracking, blocker removal, and recovery planning.

  • Serve as the central program-management point of contact among Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Validation, and Data Center teams.

  • Build and maintain integrated deployment plans, risk registers, dependency trackers, and executive-ready status reporting.

  • Drive accountability for actions, decisions, and committed dates; escalate promptly when risks exceed site-team authority or threaten delivery milestones.

  • Analyze recurring deployment issues and translate lessons learned into scalable process, readiness, and operating-model improvements.

  • Travel frequently to critical U.S. deployment sites to lead real-time coordination and accelerate issue resolution.

Qualifications

  • Demonstrated experience leading complex technical programs, deployments, infrastructure builds, or operational readiness initiatives in a data center, cloud infrastructure, hardware, manufacturing, or similarly fast-paced environment.

  • Strong ability to influence senior stakeholders and coordinate execution across multiple technical and operational functions without direct authority.

  • Proven track record of managing ambiguous, time-sensitive escalations and converting risks into actionable mitigation and recovery plans.

  • Excellent communication, prioritization, and operational judgment, including the ability to present concise updates to leadership.

  • Willingness and ability to travel frequently to U.S.-based data center deployment locations.

title: Supply Chain Coordinator
description:
Company Overview:

ADT has been in the business of helping save lives since 1874. As the #1 smart home security provider in the U.S., we help protect and connect families, businesses and larger commercial customer every day. Our continuous innovation,

advanced technology and strategic partnerships deliver products and services that help protect life and valuables, whether at home, your business or on the go. And as times change, so do we. Above all, our mission is clear: we help save lives for a living. Looking for a career where you can make a real impact? Join our team today and put purpose behind your paycheck. #WeAreADT

Check out more about life at ADT here.

Major Responsibilities:
The Supply Chain Coordinator will work within a warehouse in a designated ADT Consumer Small Business (CSB) office and will be responsible for timely and cost-effectively ordering supplies, receipt and stocking of inventory, and shipping of inventory.

The Supply Chain Coordinator ensures the security and accountability of inventory by documenting transactions using computer-based systems such as Oracle and Perpetual Inventory, processes transactions in accordance with procedures established by ADT and Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) guidelines, and periodically conducts physical inventories and system reviews.

Responsibilities & Qualifications:

  • Completes online orders for hardware, cable, and other miscellaneous items as required for the ADT Consumer Small Business (CSB) office for the Service and Installation departments and processes purchase orders to maintain the inventory levels in the SSO warehouse.
  • Ensures that the local (CSB) warehouse is a safe, organized, and secure facility and takes immediate corrective action necessary to regain compliance when defaults are found.
  • On a daily basis, uses the Perpetual Inventory functionality to document transactions on equipment to and from various sub-inventories assuring that the physical inventory and the "booked" inventory in the system match and investigates and resolves any discrepancies.
  • Pulls and issues hardware as required for Residential, Small Business and/or Core Commercial installation and service jobs as required.
  • Replenishes truck stock for each fleet vehicle and moves material from shipping/distribution trucks into the warehouse.
  • Opens shipments and verifies parts ordered, unpacks, removes, and reconciles items for each department, and tracks and forwards receipt for materials purchased to Accounts.
  • Identifies shelf locators to be entered into the Perpetual Inventory system and stocks all warehouse shelves in accordance with established stocking levels and hardware guidelines.
  • Delivers incoming material not assigned to the warehouse to its proper destination and ensures that the inventory is properly documented into the appropriate sub-inventory.
  • Maintains product knowledge for items in stock and answers technical questions related to the work order, its number, and equipment needed.
  • Examines equipment returned from cancelled accounts to determine if the equipment should be repaired, replaced under warranty, returned to manufacturers for credit, or disposed of within Perpetual Inventory and Sarbanes-Oxley guidelines.
  • Maintain various documents in accordance with Legal's document retention policies
  • Maintains control logs and copies of all invoice transactions for material procurement and material handling as per federal, state, and local regulations.
  • Performs other duties as assigned by Management.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • Education: High School Diploma. College degree preferred.
  • Experience: Preferred 3 years of material handling and inventory control experience.
  • Experience working with a computerized, perpetual inventory management system
  • Strong computer skills, (e.g., Microsoft Office, especially in excel)
  • Working knowledge of perpetual inventory management system
  • Attention to detail
  • Good verbal and written communication skills
  • Ability to operate warehouse related equipment
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs
  • Ability to climb a ladder
  • Valid driver's license

Pay and Benefits Disclosure

The pay range for this role is $19.65- $32.24 an hour and is based on experience and qualifications. We offer employees access to healthcare benefits, a 401(k) plan and company match, short-term and long-term disability coverage, life insurance, wellbeing benefits and paid time off among others. Employees accrue up to 120 hours in their first year. Your accrual rate increases after your first year. We also offer 6 paid holidays.
