title: Vice President, Global Workplace Experience
description:
Newmark Group, Inc. (Nasdaq: NMRK), together with its subsidiaries (“Newmark”), is a world leader in commercial real estate, seamlessly powering every phase of the property life cycle. Newmark’s comprehensive suite of services and products is uniquely tailored to each client, from owners to occupiers, investors to founders, and startups to blue-chip companies. Combining the platform’s global reach with market intelligence in both established and emerging property markets, Newmark provides superior service to clients across the industry spectrum. For the twelve months ended June 30, 2026, Newmark generated revenues of more than $3.6 billion. As of June 30, 2026, Newmark and its business partners together operated from over 195 offices with more than 10,000 professionals across four continents. To learn more, visit nmrk.com or follow @newmark.

Job Summary

Newmark is seeking a Vice President, Global Workplace Experience to build, lead, and grow a differentiated Workplace Experience program within the firm’s Facilities Management and Occupier Solutions business.

This senior leader will develop scalable, hospitality-led workplace experience solutions that enhance the employee, occupant, and client experience while supporting account growth and overall Facilities Management revenue objectives. Although the program will initially focus on the Americas, the role carries a global title and will help establish the standards, operating models, technology approach, and service delivery capabilities that can support future expansion.

The ideal candidate brings deep experience leading high-touch workplace experience and hospitality programs across complex, multi-site environments. They will pair a hospitality-first mindset with a practical understanding of corporate real estate and facilities operations, enabling them to create integrated solutions that are operationally sound, commercially compelling, and responsive to client needs.

Build and grow the program

  • Lead the development, refinement, and growth of Newmark’s Workplace Experience offering within Facilities Management and Occupier Solutions.
  • Create a scalable, hospitality-led service model that integrates employee experience, workplace operations, client care, and appropriate light Facilities Management coordination.
  • Establish the program’s value proposition, service architecture, operating standards, implementation methodologies, playbooks, staffing approaches, training materials, and reporting framework.
  • Develop client-facing materials, program descriptions, service scopes, and solution narratives that clearly articulate Newmark’s differentiated Workplace Experience offering.
  • Support the growth of existing Facilities Management accounts by identifying and developing Workplace Experience expansion opportunities.
  • Partner with FM leadership, Business Development, Account Management, and regional teams on new client pursuits, strategic presentations, solution development, and client-facing advisory conversations.
  • Contribute to overall FM business growth by helping position Workplace Experience as an account-expansion and differentiated service-delivery capability.

Design integrated service offerings

  • Develop and maintain two connected Workplace Experience offerings:
    • An integrated Workplace Experience solution that complements Newmark’s full Facilities Management delivery model.
    • A standalone Workplace Experience/FM-light solution for clients that require a high-quality workplace and hospitality program with coordination of select facilities activities.
  • Define standardized scopes, staffing models, pricing guidance, implementation plans, operating playbooks, and sales materials for both offerings.
  • Ensure the FM-light solution can be adapted to diverse workplace environments, including client-managed offices, landlord-managed buildings, regional portfolios, and enterprise locations.
  • Incorporate service coordination, work-order management, first-line vendor oversight, workplace issue resolution, and landlord interface management where applicable.
  • Partner closely with core FM teams to ensure clear responsibilities, seamless service handoffs, and appropriate escalation for technical maintenance, compliance, capital projects, and full FM accountability.

Lead client strategy and delivery excellence

  • Partner with account leadership, regional operations, FM teams, client-care professionals, and client stakeholders to develop workplace experience strategies aligned with business, employee, cultural, operational, and real estate objectives.
  • Serve as a senior advisor and escalation point for priority Workplace Experience accounts, complex mobilizations, program enhancements, and strategic client initiatives.
  • Build trusted relationships with senior client stakeholders and position Newmark as an advisor on hospitality-led workplace operations, employee experience, workplace service delivery, and FM-light coordination.
  • Establish required Workplace Experience standards, playbooks, service metrics, and training expectations for participating programs and accounts.
  • Drive consistency in service quality, operating procedures, implementation practices, client reporting, and employee/occupant experience across the Americas.
  • Collaborate with Facilities Management, Client Care, Strategic Advisory, Project Management, Property Management, Business Development, and other Occupier Solutions teams to deliver integrated client solutions.

Establish performance standards and insights

  • Define, implement, and monitor Workplace Experience KPIs, dashboards, and reporting standards across client programs.
  • Track and evaluate client satisfaction, employee and occupant satisfaction, service-level performance, work-order response and completion, vendor performance, staffing efficiency, workplace utilization, account expansion, revenue growth, and other operational outcomes.
  • Use performance data, client feedback, employee feedback, and market insight to identify opportunities to improve service quality, operating efficiency, employee experience, and client visibility.
  • Establish practical governance and review mechanisms that enable account teams and regional leaders to act on program performance and improvement opportunities.

Shape technology and innovation

  • Serve as the senior subject-matter advisor on workplace experience applications, digital employee-experience tools, and workplace experience measurement.
  • Shape business requirements, assess workplace experience technology options, and advise client and account teams on solutions such as visitor management, room and desk booking, workplace communications, service concierge tools, amenity and event platforms, feedback tools, and workplace experience dashboards.
  • Partner with Technology, Data, and other subject-matter experts to define metrics, reporting requirements, data standards, and workplace experience dashboards.
  • Support the adoption of automation, analytics, AI-enabled tools, and digital platforms that improve workplace experience, service consistency, client visibility, and operational effectiveness.
  • Provide strategic and operational guidance on technology; technical selection, integration, deployment, systems support, and administration will remain with Technology, Data, and designated specialists.

Lead through influence

  • Operate effectively in a matrixed organization, partnering with FM account teams, Client Care professionals, regional operations leaders, Technology, Data, Business Development, and other shared functions.
  • Build Workplace Experience capability through training, onboarding, coaching, toolkits, and practical implementation support for account and operational teams.
  • Foster a high-performance, hospitality-driven, client-focused culture across participating teams and markets.
  • Influence senior internal leaders and client stakeholders through strong executive communication, facilitation, relationship management, and operational credibility.
  • Contribute to thought leadership, market engagement, and client-facing content that strengthens Newmark’s visibility and differentiation in Workplace Experience.
  • May perform other duties as assigned.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Hospitality, Business, Corporate Real Estate, Facilities Management, Operations, Design, or a related field. Advanced degree or relevant professional certification is preferred.
  • 12+ years of progressive experience in workplace experience, hospitality, employee experience, corporate real estate, facilities management, or enterprise service delivery.
  • Deep, demonstrated background in hospitality-led workplace experience is required, including high-touch service delivery, front-of-house operations, concierge or guest services, employee engagement, amenities, community programming, events, or related services.
  • Experience building, scaling, or transforming multi-site Workplace Experience, hospitality, or integrated service-delivery programs.
  • Strong understanding of corporate real estate and workplace operations, with the ability to connect hospitality-led experiences to practical facilities, operational, and client-account requirements.
  • Experience developing standardized service models, operating standards, playbooks, implementation methodologies, training programs, staffing approaches, and performance-management processes.
  • Experience supporting strategic client pursuits, executive presentations, service scoping, account expansion, and solution development; direct sales leadership is valuable but not the primary requirement.
  • Strong aptitude for workplace experience technology, employee-facing digital platforms, workplace metrics, dashboards, analytics, automation, and AI-enabled service improvements.
  • Willingness and ability to travel domestically and internationally based on client, team, and business needs.

Working Conditions: Normal working conditions with the absence of disagreeable elements

title: Senior Research Administrator
description:
The Division of Population Sciences seeks a Senior Research Administrator to work in the McGraw/Patterson Center for Population Sciences. This growing and innovative center is committed to population-based research as a means to detect cancer early, prevent cancer at the community-based level, identify and evaluate cancer risk in high-risk populations, and measure the quality and outcomes of cancer therapy.

The Senior Research Administrator will provide grants management support to the faculty in the Division Population Sciences. The award-winning Population Sciences business office includes research administrators, administrative assistants, and program managers from diverse backgrounds with unique experience and expertise. The business office works collaboratively to support faculty conducting dry lab research and we are seeking motivated help to grow our team.

The Senior Research Administrator is responsible for the management of complex research portfolios for multiple laboratories and completes work autonomously, updating the department administrator as necessary. The Senior RA serves in a leadership role within the department business office, functioning as a senior resource to peers within the department and across the Institute.The Senior Research Administrator is responsible for a diverse set of funding types including federal, industry, foundation, donor, institutional, chargeback, and clinical trials. The Senior Research Administrator collaborates with and advises faculty and researchers on the preparation of sponsored research applications and/or the financial management of sponsored and institutional funds; and is responsible for problem solving on behalf of the department. The Senior Research Administrator has advanced and specialized expertise and regularly provides guidance and mentorship to colleagues with less experience, in addition to leading training and educational efforts within the Institute.The Senior Research Administrator is responsible for collaborating with Institute central offices such as Research Finance, Accounts Payable, Research Administration, Special Funds, Grants and Contracts, the Clinical Trials Office, Office of General Counsel, and the Innovations Office.In addition to grant management responsibilities, the Senior Research Administrator will manage special projects /assignments either within the department or across departments and will represent the Department at Institutional Committees/ Workgroups. The Senior Research Administrator is expected to partner with Department Leadership and Faculty to set strategy and provide guidance and expertise.

Located in Boston and the surrounding communities, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute is a leader in life changing breakthroughs in cancer research and patient care. We are united in our mission of conquering cancer, HIV/AIDS and related diseases. We strive to create an inclusive, diverse, and equitable environment where we provide compassionate and comprehensive care to patients of all backgrounds, and design programs to promote public health particularly among high-risk and underserved populations. We conduct groundbreaking research that advances treatment, we educate tomorrow's physician/researchers, and we work with amazing partners, including other Harvard Medical School-affiliated hospitals.

title: AOC/IOC - AS Senior Instructor/Content Developer
description:
AOC/IOC-AS Senior Instructor/Content Developer

***This position requires an active TS/SCI clearance. ***

AOC/IOC-AS Senior Instructor/Content Developer Develops, maintains, and / or delivers training material to drive intelligence goals, objectives, tradecraft, and standards. Provides lesson plans / presentations / curricula in support of educational goals and maintains materiel within the assigned educational system (i.e. AGILE, Training Development Capability (TDC), etc.). Reviews emerging policy and doctrine publications, provides feedback, and assesses for incorporation into training products. Develops / maintains training records and tracking systems as required or designated by the Government.

Compensation & Benefits:

Full time benefits include Medical, Dental, Vision, 401K and other possible benefits as provided. Benefits are subject to change with or without notice.

AOC/IOC-AS Senior Instructor/Content Developer Responsibilities Include:

  • Conduct coordination with the AOC/ IOC-AS Course Manager and the All Source Working Group members for all aspects of IOC-AS course changes and updates; responsible for the synchronization and nesting of course material associated with the training trajectory courses for AOC-AS.

  • Manages the hands on, day-to-day accountability of AOC/ IOC-AS courses instruction and delivery.

  • Create course content based on AOC-AS Course Manager and Working Group inputs.

  • Accountable for creating, editing, managing, and maintaining lesson plans, practical exercises, testable material (test bank), full Training Support Packages (TSPs), and standard operating procedures (SOPs).

  • Synchronize input from the AOC-AS Course Manager and 353T/35T Working Group members.

  • Work directly with the AOC-AS Course Manager and the 353T/35T Working Group members to assess current and future course material.

  • Assists in the development, execution, updates, and continual evolution of the IOC-AS training trajectory courses through working groups, emerging technologies and AAR reviews.

  • Accountable for instructing, providing instruction assistance, and appropriate scenario development for all courses under the IOC-AS.

  • Coordinate and facilitate training and instruction in large and small group settings with units across the enterprise.

  • Support exercises and training in a variety of instructional environments to include classrooms, MTT locations (requires travel to external customer/military sites), video-teleconferences, virtual training sessions, team teaching environments, and collective active learning environments.

AOC/IOC-AS Senior Instructor/Content Developer Experience, Education, Skills, Abilities requested:

  • Current TS/SCI security clearance

  • Minimum twelve (12) years of Army Military Intelligence experience and experience related to the specific labor category with at least a portion of the experience within the last 2 years

  • Minimum of 12 years as an MOS 35F (All-Source Analyst) DCGS-A or DIS All-Source Analyst or equivalent experience as an All-Source Analyst on DCGS-A or DIS spanning MICO, BCT, DIV-Corps level echelons.

  • Minimum of 2 years as an instructor on the DCGS-A or DIS system.

  • Graduate of the Army Basic Instructor Course (ABIC) or equivalent Intelligence Community instructor course (i.e., NGA College, NSA ADET, etc.)

  • Proficiency in DCGS-A or DIS software applications.

  • Preferred: Master’s degree

  • Must attend and graduate DISFC, GEP, and DISMGC within 12 months

  • In-depth knowledge and understanding of the Instructor/Content Developer activities required to meet mission requirements

  • Demonstrates in-depth analysis of analytic operations and knowledge management issues across organizational and intra-IC boundaries and clearly articulates key findings

  • Ability to communicate understanding from information that may be incomplete, indirect, highly complex, seemingly unrelated, and / or technically advanced

  • Ability to structure analysis based on trends in reporting and a range of analytic perspectives from other analysts, organizations, and intelligence disciplines

  • Ability to work independently with minimal oversight and direction

title: Planner, Inventory Planning
description:
Overview:

The Planner, Inventory Planning supports the global finished goods inventory planning cycle for assigned categories. The role executes planning activities across new product readiness, finished goods purchasing support, allocation follow-up, reporting, and cross-functional communication. The Planner is accountable for accurate analysis, timely execution, and issue escalation that enables the business to place the right product in the right Zone at the right time while maintaining healthy inventory productivity.

Key Accountabilities:

Portfolio Planning and Purchasing Support

  • Maintain planning inputs for assigned products, including sales forecasts, inventory policies, receipt assumptions, open orders, and availability risks.
  • Support target inventory recommendations at global and zonal level using agreed planning rules, productivity objectives, and business priorities.
  • Create and maintain purchase order recommendations with Supply teams; track receipt timing and escalate delays or data gaps.
  • Project inventory landing for the assigned scope over a rolling 12-18 month horizon.

Inventory Allocation and Zone Execution

  • Prepare and validate allocation recommendations to Zones based on sales, safety stock targets, launch priorities, and availability constraints.

  • Monitor Zone inventory positions, exceptions, and service risks; summarize proposed actions for manager review.
  • Partner with regional Supply Chain teams on operational allocation questions and issue resolution.
  • Coordinate with Distribution and Logistics partners to support smooth inventory flow for priority categories.

New Product and Lifecycle Support

  • Support weekly tracking for new and upcoming launches in assigned categories.
  • Partner with Industrial, Supply, Merchandising, and regional teams to monitor receipt readiness, launch allocation, availability, and early sell-through.
  • Maintain launch reporting and identify operational risks that require decision-making or cross-functional escalation.

Reporting, Data Quality and Continuous Improvement

  • Create recurring reporting and ad hoc analysis to support purchasing, allocation, and inventory decisions.
  • Validate core data inputs and highlight inconsistencies, missing information, or process gaps.
  • Contribute to simplification of reports, documentation of planning rules, and adoption of planning tools.

Required Qualifications:

  • 0-3 years of experience in demand planning, forecasting, supply planning, or a closely related analytical role
  • Strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel (data structuring, analysis, and reporting), Power BI, and planning tools
  • College degree and/or equivalent business experience
  • Curiosity for data quality, process improvement, and documentation for planning standards

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in a multi-category, multi-channel, or multi-region retail environment
  • Experience with Anaplan or other planning/reporting tools
  • Curious and adaptable to emerging technologies, including AI-driven tools, to enhance planning effectiveness and business insights

The hiring range for this position ranges from $94,000-$110,000. The rate of pay offered will be dependent upon candidates’ relevant skills and experience.

title: Commercieel Medewerker Binnendienst
description:
Commercieel Medewerker Binnendienst | 32-40 uur in Baarn
Bij Mees Makelaardij (onderdeel van Merel Vastgoedbeheer) zoeken we een Commercieel Medewerker Binnendienst die blij wordt van structuur, klantcontact en dingen gewoon goed regelen. Dit is geen remote of hybride functie. Het echte werk gebeurt bij ons op kantoor: schakelen, sparren en samen meters maken. Daar zit de energie.

Wat maakt deze rol leuk?

Omdat jij een centrale rol speelt in het commerciële proces. Jij bent:

  • Het eerste aanspreekpunt voor huurders en kopers.

  • De planner van bezichtigingen, inspecties en opleveringen.

  • Degene die ervoor zorgt dat overeenkomsten kloppen.

  • De bewaker van het CRM.

  • De steun en toeverlaat van onze makelaars.

  • Dankzij jou houden we overzicht, rust en resultaat in het proces.

Hoe ziet je dag eruit?

  • Je beantwoordt vragen van (potentiële) huurders en kopers.

  • Je plant afspraken strak in de agenda’s.

  • Je stelt huur- en koopovereenkomsten op.

  • Je screent huurkandidaten en begeleidt het verhuurproces.

  • Je verwerkt huuropzeggingen en mutaties netjes in de systemen.

  • Je zorgt dat onze woningen online perfect gepresenteerd staan (Funda, socials, etc.).

  • Je houdt alle leads en dossiers actueel in het CRM.

  • En je springt bij waar nodig, want samen maken we het verschil.

  • Geen dag is hetzelfde. En dat is precies waarom jij dit leuk vindt.

Waar kom je terecht?

In een professioneel en gezellig team in Baarn. Binnen Merel Vastgoedbeheer werken we met 15 betrokken collega’s, waarvan 5 bij Mees Makelaardij. We werken met korte lijnen, duidelijke communicatie en veel betrokkenheid. We houden van aanpakken, maar ook van een goede sfeer. Hier ben je geen nummer. Hier ben je een belangrijke schakel. Merel Vastgoedbeheer is een jonge vastgoedbeheerorganisatie en verantwoordelijk voor het volledige beheer van een portefeuille van ruim 3.000 duurzame, jonge en nieuwe huurwoningen in Nederland.

Ons team en onze cultuur
In ons karakteristieke kantoor in Baarn werk je samen met een gedreven en betrokken team. We zijn makkelijk bereikbaar met het openbaar vervoer en hebben een bos als overbuur, ideaal voor een frisse lunchwandeling of een goed gesprek buiten de vergaderkamer. We geloven in een open, vriendelijke werksfeer waar samenwerking en persoonlijke groei centraal staan. Of je nu op kantoor zit of een projectlocatie bezoekt: we zetten samen de schouders eronder.

Wie zoeken we?

Iemand die energie krijgt van mensen en van overzicht. Je:

  • communiceert vriendelijk en professioneel;

  • blijft rustig als het druk wordt;

  • werkt nauwkeurig (ja, écht nauwkeurig 😉);

  • denkt commercieel mee;

  • pakt snel dingen op;

  • neemt initiatief;

  • hoeft geen 20 jaar ervaring te hebben, wel de juiste mindset.

  • Je hebt mbo+ of hbo werk- en denkniveau. Misschien heb je commerciële economie, vastgoed & makelaardij of een administratieve opleiding gedaan of misschien heb je het vooral in de praktijk geleerd. Allebei is goed.

  • Je hebt feeling met vastgoed. Met verhuren. Met mensen helpen. Met processen die gewoon goed moeten lopen. Ervaring bij een makelaarskantoor, in vastgoedbeheer of in een commerciële binnendienst? Dat is mooi meegenomen. Maar belangrijker is dat je snapt hoe je overzicht houdt en service levert.

  • Systemen schrikken jou niet af. Je vindt het juist fijn als alles netjes in het CRM staat en iedereen weet waar hij aan toe is. Werk je al met vastgoedsystemen? Top. Nog niet? Dan leer je dat bij ons heel snel.

  • Je schakelt makkelijk tussen telefoontjes, mailtjes, afspraken en administratie.

Wat bieden wij? Uitstekende arbeidsvoorwaarden:

  • Een bruto maandsalaris tussen € 2.500,- en € 3.750,- afhankelijk van kennis en ervaring.

  • Ruimte voor doorgroei en persoonlijke ontwikkeling.

  • Samen werken op kantoor is voor deze functie de standaard; thuiswerken is niet mogelijk.

  • Werkgeluk zit in ons DNA: We waarderen en stimuleren nieuwe ideeën en initiatieven.

  • Balans en uitdaging: We bieden een gezonde werk-privébalans én volop kansen om jezelf te ontwikkelen.

  • Flexibele werktijden: Kies wat bij je past: 32, 36 of 40 uur per week. Wil je 36 uur werken? Dat kan in 4,5 dag per week of met om de week een dag vrij, 4x9 is bij ons niet mogelijk.

  • Veel vrije tijd: Je krijgt 30 vakantiedagen op fulltime basis.

  • Pensioen via a.s.r.: Zonder verplichte eigen bijdrage, met de mogelijkheid om extra te beleggen.

  • Pauze in het groen: Ons kantoor ligt tegenover het bos – perfect voor een ontspannen wandeling.

  • Dagelijks vers bereid eten: Onze chef-kok zorgt voor een heerlijke, gezonde lunch.

Klinkt dit als jouw volgende stap?
Dan maken we graag kennis met je. Reageer via de link en we plannen snel een gesprek. Wil je eerst even sparren met onze recruiter? Stuur gerust een app naar 06 - 12 70 26 58. Voor indiensttreding vragen we om een Verklaring Omtrent Gedrag (VOG) en een relevante referentie. Niet spannend, wel zorgvuldig.

title: Employment Policy & Compliance Consultant
description:
If you're ready to be part of our legacy of hope and innovation, we encourage you to take the first step and explore our current job openings. Your best is waiting to be discovered.

Day - 08 Hour (United States of America)

This is a Stanford Health Care job.

A Brief Overview
The HR Employment Policy & Compliance Consultant supports Stanford Health Care's employment compliance initiatives by implementing compliance programs, conducting routine assessments and providing guidance on HR policies and regulatory requirements. This role will be assigned a specific compliance area specialty(s) while maintaining broad knowledge across the full spectrum of HR compliance to help ensure the organization maintains compliance with applicable regulations across its hospital and ambulatory settings.

Locations
Stanford Health Care

What you will do

  • Manages assigned compliance area specialties (such as wage-and-hour, AWS, regulatory surveys, unemployment claims, PAGA analysis, or policy governance) while maintaining broad knowledge across the full spectrum of HR compliance.

  • Facilitates Alternative Work Schedule (AWS) elections, ensuring adherence to state regulations for accurate and timely employee communications, proper documentation, voting processes, and ensuring all requirements are met for successful implementation.

  • Conducts regular audits of meal and rest break waivers, timekeeping practices, and timecards, identifying non-compliance trends and recommending corrective actions.

  • Monitors, summarizes, and communicates legislative updates relevant to HR policies and practices, recommending policy revisions to maintain compliance with changing laws.

  • Supports PAGA case analysis by gathering relevant data and documentation, identifying potential compliance vulnerabilities, and participating in mitigation planning.

  • Represents HR in regulatory surveys and accreditation activities, preparing and organizing required documentation and supporting leadership through the process.

  • Processes and analyzes unemployment claims, providing recommendations based on case merit and compliance requirements.

  • Partners with Legal, Compliance, Risk and Operations to implement programs that mitigate risks across HR practices and delivers training on compliance best practices.


Education Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree required, preferably in Human Resources, or Business Administration from an accredited college or university.


Experience Qualifications

  • Minimum of 7 years of HR compliance or employee-relations experience required, preferably in a healthcare setting, handling multiple of the following: wage-and hour issues, Alternative Work Schedule, policy governance management of regulatory surveys, PAGA, timekeeping audits or unemployment claims.


Required Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Knowledge of healthcare regulatory requirements, including The Joint Commission standards and labor laws applicable to healthcare settings.

  • Understanding of HR policies, procedures, and best practices in compliance management.

  • Strong attention to detail and analytical skills for identifying compliance issues and recommending solutions.

  • Proficient in data collection, analysis, and reporting using HR systems and tools.

  • Effective written and verbal communication skills for explaining complex compliance requirements to various audiences.

  • Ability to work independently while supporting team objectives and collaborating with stakeholders.

  • Experience with audit processes and documentation standards.

  • Strong organizational skills with ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.


Licenses and Certifications

  • Professional certifications such as SHRM-CP, PHR, or related compliance certifications are preferred.

These principles apply to ALL employees:

SHC Commitment to Providing an Exceptional Patient & Family Experience

Stanford Health Care sets a high standard for delivering value and an exceptional experience for our patients and families. Candidates for employment and existing employees must adopt and execute C-I-CARE standards for all of patients, families and towards each other. C-I-CARE is the foundation of Stanford’s patient-experience and represents a framework for patient-centered interactions. Simply put, we do what it takes to enable and empower patients and families to focus on health, healing and recovery.

You will do this by executing against our three experience pillars, from the patient and family’s perspective:

title: Social Services and Admissions Assistant
description:
Social Service and Admissions Assistant


Pay Range:

$21.52 - $28.60

Monday - Friday, 8:30 AM - 5:00 PM, plus rotating on-call weekends


Summary:

This position supports the delivery of social services to Transitional Care (TC) patients and their families. It provides administrative support to the Director of Admissions for Supportive Living. This position helps implement the Crestwood, Woodland Park, and Oak Lea (TC) admissions processes and sales strategies to meet SL occupancy goals. This position helps the Transitional Care Admissions and Discharge Manager ensure that the Social Services Sections of the MDS, CAAs, and Care Plans are up to date. Responsible for assisting with residents' advocacy, care planning, and the discharge process. Participates in assessing residents and ensures an appropriate individualized service plan. Responsible for completing and distributing the TC admission paperwork and supporting new patient referral review, when needed. Works collaboratively with other professionals and supports the Director of Admissions - SL in delivering services that support the mission, vision, and values of VMRC.

Position


A. Essential Functions – Operations and Administration

1. Supports the integration of social services in TC and CLC that promote a patient/resident centered approach and systems continuity.

2. Completes work efficiently and accurately to maintain VMRC’s occupancy goals for Supportive Living. This includes supporting SL pre-admission tours, paperwork, and correspondence.

3. Integrates social services that promote the resident-centered approach and systems continuity.

4. Records social history, trauma-informed care, MDS, and other relevant data into the EMR system. This information supports the Care Plan and CAA implementation.

5. Assists with communicating Notice of Medicare Non-Coverage (NOMNC) information to skilled patients.

6. Assists with timely and accurate completion and distribution of Supportive Living admission paperwork with patients and/or responsible parties.

7. Participates in scheduled team, service line, and organizational meetings.

8. Participates in the Supportive Living referral and move-in process without the Director of Admissions and/or the Transitional Care Admissions and Discharge Manager.

9. Assists with follow-up phone calls to patients following discharge and tracks responses as indicated.

10. Assists in ordering, tracking, and delivering DME.

11. Assists with insurance communication with patients and stakeholders.

12. Communicates thoroughly and effectively both in writing and verbally, with others who impact patient/resident care, including but not limited to coworkers, supervisors, patients, providers, referral sources, families, and insurance groups.


B. Essential Functions – Supportive Living Occupancy Management

1. Support the Director of Admissions – Supportive Living during the move-in process.

2. Involved in the marketing, promotion, and sales of Supportive Living and professionally representing VMRC to external stakeholders.

3. Effectively communicates with internal stakeholders about vacancies, move-ins, move-outs, patient/resident needs and trends to meet or exceed occupancy goals.

4. Provides Supportive Living tours and responds to telephone and online inquiries from prospective residents as needed.

5. Coordinates with Director of Admissions – Supportive Living to support admission paperwork and procedures while maintaining consistency and standardization.

6. Proactively develops customer relationships by listening to, understanding, anticipating, and providing solutions to customer needs.

7. Actively participates in service activities as requested by supervisor.


C. Essential Functions – Patient/Resident Centered Care

1. Collaborates with multi-disciplinary staff for resident care planning and services, communicating and coordinating treatment approaches, including behavior management, with patients/residents, family, and staff.

2. Promotes staff actions that maintain or enhance each patient's/resident’s dignity and individual rights, creating a homelike environment.

3. Builds relationships with patients/residents and their families/significant others; maintains ongoing communication concerning the patients/residents’ needs and changing health status.

4. Coordinate the equipment needs of patients prior to discharge (walkers, wheelchairs, etc.).

5. Assists with both short-term and long-term care insurance claims.

6. Actively engages patients/residents and provides emotional and social support.

7. Champion’s patient/resident centered care.


D. Essential Functions – Resident Assessment

1. Conduct MDS assessments that comply with the Resident Assessment Instrument (RAI) accurately and on time.

2. Provides psychosocial assessment (cognitive and mood patterns) upon resident move-in and at periodic intervals, thus promoting the understanding of individual patients/residents.

3. Maintains an ongoing assessment of patient/resident needs, planning services to meet these needs.

4. Assesses with patients/residents, families, and staff the best room and/or roommate placement and coordinates any changes.

5. Provides Life Enrichment assessment.


E. Essential Functions – Patient/Resident Focused Problem Solving

1. Assists in overseeing and monitoring the adjustment of the resident and family following move-in, and during other personal adjustments due to significant changes such as the patient’s/resident's medical condition, death/loss issues, etc.

2. Assists with planning and coordinating applicable move-out processes.

3. Adapts the environment to facilitate patient/resident optimal adjustment and oversees arrangements for adaptive equipment, clothing, and personal items.

4. Assists patients/residents with financial and legal matters, referring to appropriate community resources.

5. Assists in managing patient/resident complaints/grievances as stated in the Resident Agreement.

6. Assists in overseeing the missing item process and ensuring investigation, resolution/closure, and tracking.


F. General

1. Complies with all VMRC and service line policies & guidelines conscientiously.

2. Actively engages residents in a meaningful, positive, and compassionate manner while ensuring an environment of resident-centered respect and appreciation.

3. Maintains confidentiality of all resident care and protected health information. Reports known or suspected incidents of unauthorized disclosure of confidential information to supervisor or designee.

4. Handles responsibility and maintains a positive, professional, collaborative working relationship with residents, families, administration, peers, and co-workers.

5. Uses correct body mechanics to prevent injury to self, residents, and other staff.

6. Assumes responsibility for and actively participates in staff development (professional growth) and continuing education to keep skills and required certification(s) up-to-date.

7. Demonstrates computer skills necessary to complete job tasks/responsibilities.

8. Attends all required in-services and service line staff meetings.

9. Follows emergency and evacuation procedures.

10. Performs other duties as assigned by supervisor.

Summary of Physical, Sensory, Environmental and Other Requirements Needed to

Perform the Essential Functions of this Job


A. Work Environment

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally exposed to dust, fumes, odors, and airborne particles, as well as to biological and chemical hazards and mechanical equipment.


B. Position Type/Expected Hours of Work

This position operates in an office setting and regularly visits patients/residents in their rooms. It routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, and fax machines. The routine work schedule is during business hours; however, occasional after-hours needs may require scheduling flexibility. Additionally, on-call responsibilities are expected for referrals and admissions.


C. Access to Confidential Information

This position has access to patient/resident medical records as needed to perform essential functions.


E. Supervisor Responsibility

This position does not have supervisory responsibilities or the authority to determine who can access confidential information.

title: Per Diem Administrator - Master of Health Administration Program
description:
The Associate Administrative Director of the Master of Health Administration (MHA) program provides coordinated leadership for the program’s applied learning, student advising, mentorship, fellowship development, capstone/culminating experience, and professional formation activities. The role integrates functions currently distributed across multiple individuals, including the capstone, revised culminating experience, mentorship program, selected course responsibilities, and general advisement.

Working closely with the MHA Director, Vice Chair for Research and Education in the Department of Public Health, PHHA administrative team, MHA faculty, the APE Coordinator, Career Services staff, student affairs, admissions, alumni, mentors, preceptors, and other partners, the Associate Administrative Director strengthens the coherence of the student experience and supports the program’s positioning as a practice-oriented MHA grounded in academic medical center leadership.

Applied Learning and Culminating Experience

Coordinate the MHA capstone sequence and revised culminating experience.

Work with faculty, preceptors, mentors, the APE Coordinator, and program leadership to align projects and placements with program competencies and applied healthcare management practice.

Support students in identifying project topics, applied learning sites, mentors, placements, and deliverables.

Coordinate with the APE Coordinator on placement processes, site expectations, student preparation, and documentation.

Monitor student progress and recommend improvements based on outcomes, feedback, and assessment findings.

Mentorship, Professional Development, and Fellowship Development

Manage and refine the yearlong MHA mentorship program in coordination with Career Services staff and program leadership.

Match students with mentors based on professional goals, interests, and mentor availability.

Establish expectations for mentor/mentee engagement and collect feedback for annual improvement.

Expand the mentor network through alumni, faculty, health system leaders, and healthcare management contacts.

Coordinate with Career Services staff on mentorship programming, professional development workshops, career-readiness activities, employer engagement, and student preparation.

Lead development of a funded MHA fellowship program within Mount Sinai, including potential host departments, funding models, selection criteria, timelines, student preparation, and placement coordination.

Identify additional post-graduate fellowship or administrative residency pathways with health system, academic medical center, affiliated, and external healthcare partners.

Track student interest, employer engagement, placement activity, and fellowship-related outcomes.

Student Advising and Professional Formation
Advise students on course planning, program progression, applied learning, mentorship, capstone planning, fellowship preparation, and career-readiness activities.
Serve as a first-line resource for student questions related to program requirements, timelines, and professional development opportunities.
Coordinate with the MHA Director, PHHA administrative team, APE Coordinator, Career Services staff, student affairs, faculty advisors, and course instructors when additional support is needed.
Support retention, progression, and student satisfaction through proactive communication and timely follow-up.
Identify recurring student concerns and recommend improvements to advising, communication, or program operations.

Curriculum and Program Support
Help align course content, capstone expectations, mentorship activities, fellowship preparation, applied placements, and professional development experiences.
Support orientations, student events, alumni/employer panels, mentor activities, and other program-building initiatives.
Assist with gathering feedback, tracking participation, documenting outcomes, and identifying opportunities for operational improvement.
Support the MHA Director’s program evaluation and assessment work by helping collect, organize, and track relevant information related to capstone completion, applied placements, mentorship participation, student advising needs, fellowship development, and professional outcomes.
Help implement improvements identified through the MHA Director’s evaluation and assessment process, particularly in applied learning, advising, mentorship, fellowship development, placement coordination, and student communication.

Recruitment, Enrollment, and Market Positioning Support
Support the MHA Director, PHHA administrative team, admissions, enrollment management, marketing, and departmental leadership in recruitment, yield, and student engagement efforts.
Participate in recruitment events, webinars, admitted-student activities, open houses, and information sessions.
Help communicate the value of the program’s applied learning model, mentorship structure, capstone experience, fellowship development, Sinai-based opportunities, and AMC setting.
Provide student-experience perspective to recruitment materials, yield activities, pipeline development, and program positioning.
Support efforts to strengthen the MHA program’s distinctiveness in a competitive graduate health administration market.
Appointment Term

Education Requirements
Master’s degree or equivalent education and experience

Experience Requirements
7-10 years of proven management ability including:
1. Knowledge and understanding of institutional regulations, policies, and practices specific to human resources management of BU and NBU staff
2. Knowledge and understanding of medical academic, clinical, research, and practice regulatory compliance
3. Administrative planning and leadership skills, particularly in the development and implementation of complex administrative programs
4. Ability to develop successful collaborative relationships at all levels within the organization.
5. Advanced analytical, evaluative, and objective critical thinking skills.
6. Skill in examining and re-engineering operations and procedures, formulating policy, and developing and implementing new strategies and procedures.
7. Knowledge of clinical operations and/or administration in a medical school environment.
8. Working knowledge and understanding of practice productivity and performance measurement programs and systems.
9. Knowledge and understanding of facility and space management principles, processes, and techniques.
10. Knowledge of budgeting, fiscal management, and human resources management systems

title: Calibration Technician - Pittsburgh, PA
description:
Calibration Technician – Pittsburgh, PA

Pittsburgh, PA | Instrument Calibration Solutions, LLC | Service
Instrument Calibration Solutions, LLC . |
Full-time | $22.00 - $29.00 / Hour (DOE)


Position Overview


Instrument Calibration Solutions, LLC (ICS) is seeking a Calibration Technician to join our Pittsburgh, PA laboratory. This role is intended for a technician who can work independently, apply sound metrology principles, and deliver accurate, compliant calibration services in laboratory and onsite environments.


This position aligns with industry-leading calibration organizations while maintaining ICS’s culture of quality, accountability, and long-term customer partnership. Growth opportunities are available for technicians seeking to expand technical depth and responsibility.


*We are currently located in Aliquippa, PA and will be moving to Pittsburgh towards the end of 2026.


Key Responsibilities

  • Perform calibration, adjustment, troubleshooting, and repair of electronic, mechanical, electro-mechanical, and process instrumentation
  • Execute calibration work independently in the laboratory and at customer sites as assigned
  • Apply appropriate measurement techniques, uncertainty concepts, and TAR/TUR principles
  • Accurately complete calibration certificates, reports, and supporting documentation
  • Interpret customer purchase orders, specifications, and technical documentation
  • Coordinate with operations and scheduling staff to meet turnaround commitments
  • Maintain calibration standards, equipment, and work areas in a safe and organized condition
  • Interface professionally with customers to clarify requirements and answer technical questions
  • Assist with training and mentoring of junior technicians as experience allows
  • Identify potential service opportunities during customer interactions and relay internally
  • Support general laboratory operations as required

Qualifications & Experience

Required:

  • High school diploma or GED
  • Hands-on experience in a calibration laboratory, field service, or related technical environment
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality
  • Valid driver’s license and ability to travel locally as needed

Preferred:

  • Associate degree or technical training in Electronics, Metrology, or Engineering Technology
  • Experience working under ISO/IEC 17025 and/or ANSI/NCSL Z540
  • Familiarity with uncertainty budgets, statistics, and multi-discipline calibration
  • Experience with calibration software (MET/CAL, BenchTop, IndySoft, etc.)
  • ASQ CCT/CMT, PMEL, or equivalent military metrology training

Skills & Competencies

  • Strong mathematical aptitude and analytical ability
  • Proficiency with electronic and mechanical measurement equipment
  • Ability to read and interpret technical procedures and specifications
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills
  • Strong organizational and time-management skills
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook
  • Customer-focused and professional demeanor

Physical & Work Requirements

  • Ability to lift and carry up to 50 lbs regularly
  • Ability to stand, sit, walk, reach, stoop, kneel, and handle lab equipment
  • Exposure to electrical equipment and moving mechanical parts
  • Occasional work at customer facilities in industrial or laboratory environments

Benefits Offered

  • Paid Holidays
  • Paid Vacations and Sick time
  • 401k Plan
  • Health, Vision, and Dental coverage

About Us

ICS, LLC. provides complete metrology solutions for calibration and repair of electrical, mechanical, optical, and process control instruments to meet stringent documentation and quality requirements. Our calibration services meet the applicable requirements of ANSI/NCSL Z540-1 and ISO/IEC 17025, using standards with accuracies traceable to NIST or compared to nationally or internationally recognized consensus standards. ICS Inc. was founded in 2004 by seasoned Marine Corps Metrologists. ICS LLC. prides itself on quality workmanship and customer satisfaction. Our background in the United States Marine Corps calibration program gave us a high-level of knowledge in electrical and mechanical metrology.

Our staff of highly qualified calibration technicians take great pride in their work. We do it right the first time, every time, and in the process, we make sure customer needs are met, and expectations are exceeded. At ICS, LLC., we develop a relationship and partnership with our customers and take the time to listen to our customers and understand each industry. ICS, LLC. partnered with Brechbuhler Scales, Inc. in 2020 to optimize service opportunities even further.

The Buyer is a strategic merchandising leader responsible for end-to-end ownership of a defined retail category portfolio, with accountability for sales, margin, inventory productivity, product differentiation, and long-term category growth. This role sets and executes assortment strategy aligned to brand positioning, guest insights, food and consumer trends, and financial objectives while leading the product lifecycle from opportunity identification and concept development through sourcing, commercialization, launch, in-season optimization, and exit strategy.

The Buyer shapes category vision, defines assortment architecture and pricing strategy, leads vendor partnerships and negotiations, and translates market, guest, food/CPG trend, and performance insights into decisive actions that improve productivity. This role may also support branded and private label product strategies, partnering cross-functionally on product quality, packaging, claims, costing, value perception, and speed-to-market. In addition to leading through cross-functional influence, this role may directly manage and develop at least one team member, helping build merchandising capability, strengthen execution, and elevate decision-making across the team. The Buyer is expected to influence cross-functional decisions, model strong leadership, and consistently deliver profitable, brand-right growth.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Category Leadership, Assortment Strategy, and Brand Fit

  • Own a defined merchandise category or portfolio of categories, including assortment strategy, financial performance, vendor structure, and multi-season growth plans
  • Set category direction by translating guest insight, competitive intelligence, food and consumer trend analysis, and business performance into differentiated assortment strategies
  • Define assortment architecture across key item programs, replenishment, seasonal newness, opening price point, and premium offerings to maximize productivity and brand relevance

Product Development, Commercialization, and Innovation

  • Lead product development, commercialization, and curation for assigned categories, ensuring assortments are guest-right, operationally feasible, competitively positioned, and aligned with brand standards
  • Guide product formulation, packaging, quality expectations, claims, pricing, and value perception in partnership with vendors and internal stakeholders
  • Drive innovation and category evolution by identifying white space opportunities, emerging trends, brand-right product concepts, and private label opportunities that support long-term growth
  • Translate consumer, competitive, and vendor capability insights into commercially viable assortment, packaging, cost, and go-to-market recommendations

Financial Ownership and Inventory Productivity

  • Own category performance against sales, gross margin, turn, markdown, and inventory productivity targets, with accountability for balancing growth, profitability, and risk
  • Partner with Planning and Allocation to shape open-to-buy, receipt flow, item productivity, pricing architecture, and inventory investment decisions
  • Apply advanced retail math, forecasting insight, and scenario analysis to make informed decisions that improve category returns and reduce inventory exposure

In-Season Business Management

  • Lead weekly and seasonal business review processes to identify opportunities, mitigate risks, and take decisive action on reorders, cancellations, promotional strategies, markdowns, consolidations, and exits
  • Continuously evaluate SKU productivity and assortment productivity to inform future buy strategies, space allocation, and portfolio optimization
  • Own end-of-life and exit strategies for underperforming items in ways that protect margin, improve inventory health, and create space for newness

Vendor Strategy and Management

  • Lead vendor relationships for assigned categories, including strategic sourcing, negotiations, cost management, performance expectations, and long-term partnership development
  • Negotiate costs, terms, exclusivity, and product development opportunities that strengthen margin performance and support differentiated assortments
  • Evaluate vendor and co-packer capabilities across product quality, packaging execution, food safety expectations, production capacity, cost management, service levels, and speed-to-market

Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Influence cross-functional partners across Planning, Allocation, Supply Chain, Marketing, QA, Visual Merchandising, Store Operations, and eCommerce to move products from concept through launch effectively
  • Present category strategies, assortment recommendations, performance insights, and financial actions to leadership with clear business rationale and executive presence
  • Lead cross-functional initiatives and category workstreams, aligning partners around priorities, decisions, timelines, and business outcomes

People Leadership

  • Lead, coach, and develop at least one direct report, providing clear direction, ongoing feedback, and support for individual growth and performance
  • Set expectations, prioritize work, and reinforce accountability to ensure high-quality execution and strong business outcomes
  • Build team capability by sharing merchandising expertise, strengthening decision-making, and supporting development of business acumen and functional skills

Experience and Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Merchandising, Marketing, Retail Management, or related field; or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience
  • 5+ years of progressive experience in retail buying, merchandising, category management, CPG brand management, product development, or related commercial food/consumer goods functions, with increasing ownership of assortment, product, brand, or category decisions
  • Demonstrated experience owning a category or major assortment with accountability for sales, margin, inventory productivity, and vendor performance
  • Experience leading, coaching, and developing at least one direct report or comparable people leadership responsibility

Focus on You

We're all about making sure you're taken care of too. Here's what's in it for you:

  • Good Work Deserves Good Pay: Competitive Annual Salary | Annual Bonus Opportunities

  • Support That Goes Beyond the Clock: Medical, Rx, Dental and Vision Benefits on Day 1| Life Insurance and Disability Coverage | Paid Vacation/Employee Assistance Program

  • Grow and Thrive Your Way: Business Resource Groups | Tuition Reimbursement | Professional Development

  • Culture of Belonging: Support that starts on day one | Onboarding, training, and development to help you thrive | Recognition programs and employee events that bring us together

  • Invest in Your Future: 401k Plan with Company Matching Contributions at 90 days | Employee Stock Purchase Program

  • More Perks, Just Because: 35% Discount on Cracker Barrel Food and Retail items | Exclusive Biscuit Perks like discounts on home, travel, cell phones, and more!

Since 1969, Cracker Barrel has been a place to gather around delicious food, abundant servings, unexpected finds, and a warm welcome. Over time, it's become even more - somewhere folks can reconnect and feel at home. With more than 70,000 team members nationwide, we take pride in our roots -- always serving up more than a meal.

title: Senior Systems Developer, IT Enterprise
description:
Clio is the global leader in legal AI technology, empowering legal professionals and law firms of every size to work smarter, faster, and more securely.

We are transforming the legal experience for all by bettering the lives of legal professionals while increasing access to justice.

Summary:

We are looking for an experienced Senior Systems Developer with strong system analysis and integration development capabilities to join our IT Systems team, with a primary allocation to the Finance Systems team as a dedicated integrations specialist. This role combines hands-on iPaaS development with the ability to translate complex finance business requirements into structured, reliable, secure, and well-documented integration solutions, while leveraging AI to drive process automation and standardization. You will design, build, and maintain integrations connecting critical finance systems such as NetSuite, Coupa, and Leapfin, working closely with the Finance Systems team who specialize in NetSuite and Coupa.

The ideal candidate can operate independently, own integrations end to end, and work cross-functionally in a fast-paced SaaS environment. You will be expected to explore and apply AI-powered tools and techniques to accelerate development, improve process consistency, and unlock new automation opportunities across finance operations. As a steward of sensitive financial data, you will play a key role in upholding Clio’s high compliance and security standards across all integration touchpoints.

What You’ll Work On

  • Design, develop, and maintain custom integrations that connect finance systems including NetSuite, Coupa, and Leapfin, ensuring reliable, secure, and auditable data flows across the finance technology stack

  • Identify opportunities for automation across finance operations and implement solutions using code, iPaaS platforms, and AI-powered tooling to improve the velocity of Clions globally

  • Partner with the Finance Systems team as the go-to integrations expert for finance workflows such as procure-to-pay, revenue recognition, accounts payable/receivable, and general ledger processes. This includes leading requirement gathering, translating business needs into technical specifications, data flow diagrams, and field mapping documentation

  • Build event-driven automations, webhook-based triggers, and bulk data synchronization processes with robust monitoring, error handling, and retry mechanisms to ensure data consistency and production-grade reliability

  • Support integration development and testing during NetSuite, Coupa, and Leapfin implementation and enhancement projects, collaborating with consulting partners and vendors on technical integration requirements

  • Document integration architectures, data flows, API specifications, and troubleshooting procedures to support operational continuity and audit readiness

What You Bring

  • Strong expertise with iPaaS or middleware platforms such as Workato, Celigo, or Boomi, including workflow/recipe development, custom connector configuration, error handling, and performance optimization is a MUST have.

  • Practical experience in one of the following languages:

    • Ruby

    • Python

    • Golang

    • Bash

  • Direct experience working with finance systems such as NetSuite, Coupa, or Leapfin, with strong system analysis skills and a solid understanding of finance business processes including procure-to-pay, revenue recognition, accounts payable/receivable, and general ledger workflows is a MUST have.

  • Fluency in modern API standards (REST, GraphQL), authentication methods (OAuth, API tokens, SAML), and integration patterns including webhooks, event-driven architectures, bulk data processing, and data transformation

  • A strong understanding of compliance and security best practices as they relate to financial data integrations, including SOC 2 controls, data privacy, access management, and audit trail requirements

  • Demonstrated interest or hands-on experience leveraging AI tools and techniques (e.g., AI-assisted development, intelligent automation, LLM-based workflow optimization) to improve process efficiency and standardization.

  • A keen interest in improving your craft by using AI.


Bonus Points

  • Experience with iPaaS or middleware platforms (e.g., Workato, Celigo, Boomi, Okta Workflows)

  • Background working at a high-growth SaaS company

  • Experience with other enterprise systems (e.g., Workday, Salesforce, Hubspot) and a broad understanding of how they integrate within a modern finance tech stack

  • Experience supporting internal or external audit processes related to system integrations and financial data flows

  • Experience implementing AI-driven automation in a finance or enterprise systems context, such as intelligent document processing, predictive reconciliation, or AI-assisted data validation

  • Practical experience with CI/CD platforms such as GitHub Actions to support integration deployment and testing workflows

What you will find here:

Compensation is one of the main components of Clio’s Total Rewards Program. We have developed a series of programs and processes to ensure we are creating fair and competitive pay practices that form the foundation of our human and high-performing culture.

Some highlights of our Total Rewards program include:

  • Competitive, equitable salary with top-tier health benefits, dental, and vision insurance

  • Hybrid work environment, with expectation for local Clions (Vancouver, Calgary, Toronto, Dublin and Sydney) to be in office minimum twice per week.

  • Flexible time off policy, with an encouraged 20 days off per year.

  • EAP benefits for you and household members, including counseling and online resources

  • 401k matching and Child Education Savings

  • Clioversary recognition program with special acknowledgement at 3, 5, 7, and 10 years

​

The expected salary range for this role is $148,800 to $201,400 USD. Initial placement within the range is informed by geographic region, experience, and skillset, with room to progress as impact and tenure grow. Final offer amounts will vary based on candidate profile.

Diversity, Inclusion, Belonging and Equity (DIBE) & Accessibility

Our team shows up as their authentic selves, and are united by our mission. We are dedicated to diversity, equity and inclusion. We pride ourselves in building and fostering an environment where our teams feel included, valued, and enabled to do the best work of their careers, wherever they choose to log in from. title: Senior Actuary
description:
Department:

Analytics

Job Description:

The Senior Actuary, Reserving performs and supports Property & Casualty reserve analyses across multiple lines of business. This role helps ensure the accuracy, integrity, and transparency of loss and loss adjustment expense reserves through sound actuarial analysis, strong technical execution, and disciplined documentation. The Senior Actuary partners with Claims, Finance, Underwriting, and other stakeholders to evaluate reserve adequacy, monitor emerging trends, and provide insights that support financial reporting and business decision-making. This position also supports continued improvement in reserving practices, governance, and analytical capabilities.

Work Arrangement:

  • Employees who live within 30 miles of the TMG home office are expected to follow a hybrid or in-office schedule. The initial training period may require additional in‑office days.

Accountabilities:

Reserving Process: Perform and contribute to quarterly Loss and LAE reserve analyses across assigned Property & Casualty lines of business.

  • Prepare reserve analyses and recommendations using appropriate actuarial techniques and judgment.

  • Ensure reserve indications are well-supported, documented, and consistent with actuarial standards and company policies.

  • Maintain reserving models, methodologies, and supporting documentation.

  • Contribute to the development and enhancement of reserving controls, governance processes, and documentation standards.

  • Perform diagnostic testing, trend analysis, and assumption reviews to evaluate reserve adequacy.

  • Partner with Finance to support financial close processes, reserve change analyses, audits, and regulatory reporting.

  • Support external actuarial reviews, audits, and regulatory examinations as needed.

Analytics, Insights & Decision Support: Develop actuarial analyses and insights related to reserve performance, loss trends, and emerging risks.

  • Analyze development patterns, claim trends, and sources of reserve volatility.

  • Collaborate with Claims and Underwriting to understand operational and portfolio drivers impacting reserve results.

  • Perform scenario testing, reserve uncertainty assessments, and forecasting exercises.

  • Monitor emerging issues and communicate potential impacts on reserve adequacy and business performance.

  • Contribute actuarial analysis to reinsurance, capital planning, business planning, and other enterprise initiatives.

  • Contribute to enhancements in actuarial models, data processes, and analytical tools.

  • Develop and communicate clear analyses and recommendations to actuarial leadership and business partners.

Collaboration & Professional Development: Contribute to actuarial team effectiveness through strong technical execution, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

  • Collaborate with actuarial peers to review and validate work products for accuracy and consistency where appropriate.

  • Partner effectively with cross-functional stakeholders across Finance, Claims, Underwriting, and Analytics.

  • Share technical knowledge and provide informal guidance to less experienced actuarial team members.

  • Contribute to departmental initiatives focused on process improvement, efficiency, and governance.

  • Communicate actuarial concepts and analytical findings clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Pursue ongoing professional development and remain current on actuarial standards, industry trends, and reserving practices.

Qualifications:

  • 5 to 8 years of actuarial experience in Property & Casualty insurance, with significant experience in reserving.

  • ACAS required; FCAS designation or active pursuit of FCAS preferred.

  • Strong understanding of loss reserving techniques, loss development analysis, reserve uncertainty, and actuarial modeling.

  • Proficiency with modeling and data analysis tools; experience with actuarial reserving software or programming tools preferred.

  • Experience supporting financial reporting, reserve reviews, audits, or regulatory requirements.

  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and critical-thinking skills.

  • Effective written and verbal communication skills with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-actuarial audiences.

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and work independently while collaborating effectively across teams.

  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality, governance, and documentation standards.

  • Familiarity with actuarial standards of practice (ASOPs) and reserving best practices.

Pay Range:

Anticipated Hiring Range:

  • $120,000 - $180,000 annual base salary depending on experience, qualifications, and geographic location

Benefits:

We are proud to offer our full-time regular employees a robust benefits suite that includes:

  • Competitive base salary plus incentive plans for eligible team members

  • 401(K) retirement plan that includes a company match of up to 6% of your eligible salary

  • Free basic life and AD&D, long-term disability and short-term disability insurance

  • Medical, dental and vision plans to meet your unique healthcare needs

  • Wellness incentives

  • Generous time off program that includes personal, holiday and volunteer paid time off

  • Flexible work schedules and hybrid/remote options for eligible positions

  • Educational assistance

title: Supply Chain Snr Director – CPU/GPU Sourcing
description:
Oracle is seeking an experienced Supply Chain Senior Director to lead strategic sourcing across critical CPU and GPU categories supporting our infrastructure platforms.

This senior leadership role will be responsible for developing and executing sourcing strategies that support the timely, cost-effective availability of critical technologies while balancing cost, capacity, supply continuity, supplier performance, and broader operational priorities. The position will lead strategic supplier selection, complex commercial negotiations, business awards, supplier development, and performance management across CPU and GPU technologies.

The Supply Chain Senior Director will lead a team of Sourcing Managers and work closely with Engineering, Finance, Planning, Quality, and other organizations to align sourcing strategies with technology roadmaps, new platform requirements, and Oracle’s infrastructure growth. This role requires strong CPU/GPU industry and supplier expertise, commercial judgment, executive influence, and demonstrated leadership and people management skills.

Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute strategic sourcing and category strategies across CPU and GPU technologies.
  • Lead supplier assessment, selection, negotiations, business awards, supplier development, and ongoing supplier performance management.
  • Develop and maintain strong relationships with strategic suppliers, including executive-level engagement on complex commercial, capacity, performance, and supply matters.
  • Lead complex commercial negotiations involving cost, capacity, commercial terms, supplier performance, and long-term business requirements.
  • Build sourcing strategies that align supplier capabilities, capacity, commercial considerations, and technology and product roadmaps with Oracle's business requirements.
  • Partner with Engineering, Finance, Planning, Quality, and other stakeholders to align sourcing strategies and supplier decisions with new platforms and business priorities.
  • Drive sourcing strategies and business awards for new platforms while supporting supplier readiness, capacity, and continuity of supply.
  • Establish and maintain supplier performance mechanisms, operating processes, and corrective-action plans that drive accountability and continuous improvement.
  • Identify and mitigate supplier, capacity, commercial, performance, and continuity-of-supply risks across critical CPU and GPU categories.
  • Develop and implement sourcing policies, procedures, and scalable operating mechanisms that reduce costs, streamline execution, and support infrastructure growth.
  • Coordinate with Finance and other stakeholders on cost, sourcing, capacity, and related business considerations.
  • Lead, coach, develop, and evaluate a team of Sourcing Managers to ensure effective execution and continued development of the organization.
  • Direct the implementation of sourcing and operational strategies through subordinate managers while maintaining accountability for business outcomes.
  • Engage internal executives and external supplier leadership to influence decisions, negotiate difficult matters, and resolve complex commercial and operational issues.

Qualifications

  • Demonstrated senior leadership experience in strategic sourcing, procurement, global supply management, supply chain, or a related function within complex hardware or technology environments.
  • Strong functional expertise in strategic sourcing and supplier management, with experience developing and executing category strategies.
  • Strong industry, product, and supplier knowledge relevant to CPUs, GPUs, semiconductors, or closely related technologies.
  • Experience supporting hyperscale cloud, data center, AI infrastructure, or comparable technology environments.
  • Proven experience leading supplier assessment, selection, complex commercial negotiations, contracting, business awards, supplier development, and performance management.
  • Experience developing sourcing strategies that consider technology and product roadmaps, supplier capabilities, cost, capacity, competitive commercial terms, and continuity of supply.
  • Strong understanding of supplier capacity planning, performance management, risk mitigation, and scalable supply-chain execution.
  • Experience partnering with Engineering and other technical organizations to translate technology or product requirements into sourcing strategies.
  • Demonstrated ability to work across Engineering, Finance, Planning, Quality, and other organizations to influence decisions and drive alignment.
  • Demonstrated leadership and people management skills, including experience leading managers and developing high-performing teams.
  • Strong executive communication, negotiation, commercial judgment, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
  • Ability to interact effectively with executive management and supplier leadership and influence complex business and sourcing decisions.
  • Broad organizational and business knowledge with the ability to operate effectively in a rapidly changing environment.
  • BS or MS degree, or equivalent experience relevant to the functional area.

HUS Diagnostiikkakeskus on Suomen johtava kliinisten laboratorio- ja kuvantamispalvelujen tuottaja. Pääasiallinen toiminta-alueemme on HUS-yhtymän erikoissairaanhoito ja HUSiin kuuluvien hyvinvointialueiden perusterveydenhuolto. Vastaamme myös Kymenlaakson hyvinvointialueen ja Etelä-Karjalan hyvinvointialueen laboratorio- ja kuvantamistoiminnasta.

Toimimme kahdeksalla lääketieteen erikoisalalla. Vastaamme valtakunnallisesti useista erityisosaamista vaativista tutkimuksista sekä yliopistolliselle sairaalalle kuuluvasta tutkimuksesta ja opetuksesta. Diagnostiset tutkimukset ovat keskeisessä roolissa sairauksien varmistamisessa, poissulkemisessa, osana hoitoa sekä hoidon seurannassa ja seulonnassa. HUS Diagnostiikkakeskuksessa työskentelee noin 3300 laboratorio- ja kuvantamisalan asiantuntijaa yli 150 toimipisteessä.

Haemme nyt laboratoriohoitajaa näytteenoton työtehtäviin Meilahden sairaala-alueen vuodeosastonäytteenottoon. Työ on kolmivuorotyötä.

Työnkuvasi koostuu pääasiassa näytteenottotehtävistä. Työsi näytteenotossa sisältää runsaasti potilaskohtaamisia työpäivän aikana. Näytteenottajan päivittäisessä työssä tukenasi ovat ammattitaitoiset kollegat ja esihenkilöt.

Aiemman kokemuksesi huomioiden löydämme sinulle mieluisimman työpisteen näytteenottotyön aloittamiselle, ja kokemuksen karttuessa pääset työskentelemään monipuolisesti eri työpisteissä.Mikäli olet jo kokenut näytteenoton ammattilainen, saat sen mukaan vastuuta koskien työtehtäviäsi.

Näytteenottotyö on luonteeltaan hyvin itsenäistä, jossa näytteenottajalla on merkittävä rooli näytteen laadun varmistajana. Siksi panostamme yksikössämme perehdytykseen ja osaamisen kehittymisen arviointiin.
